docs.title: 2026-07-21 (later) — Grown-lists doctrine: briefs point at canon; an A/B decided the ship
docs.text:
• Canon extended, briefs slimmed (relocate, never delete). academic-writing.md B8 is now the declared canonical AI-tell catalogue (+underscore/pivotal/robust-as-filler, +tricolons-for-rhythm, +stacked hedging, +symmetric paragraph shapes). The field-learned leak-classes are codebook entries E10 (value-to-category mapping) and E11 (citation fidelity vs full text). The conformance brief points at B8; the faithfulness brief names E10/E11 and the builder EMBEDS those two blocks extracted from the codebook (generated-not-duplicated; extraction failure = INACTIVE).
  • The ship was decided by an A/B, not a feeling (KG's receiver caveat as law): same seeded paragraph (6 planted tells, 3 existing only in canon post-slim), same model, old vs new brief. Both arms 6/6 on seeds, both FAIL 1/5 — and the NEW-brief arm made the better judgement call, exonerating Kai's characteristic "X, not Y" appositive by citing exemplar CO1 under the exemplars-beat-rules precedence, where the OLD-brief arm false-flagged it off its inline list. The predicted anchoring effect, observed live.
  • Rule triage is standing doctrine (kai-writing SKILL): gate-able → gate; model-knowable → cut; neither → canonical file + pointer. Slim by RECEIVER, never by fashion; sonnet-facing scaffolding stays; brief changes ship with an A/B. Companion doctrine message to the lecture pipeline: coord prompt-budget-doctrine/001.

docs.title: 2026-07-21 (third) — Field day 2: the loop gets a diagnosis, not just a budget
docs.text:
• kai-writing: the SAME-CLASS CIRCUIT BREAKER (pn F12, KG's verdict: "you should have notified me earlier... did not make sense to iterate so much"). A live paragraph took FIVE rounds — four symptoms of ONE unsettled spec question; the cap of 4 counts rounds but cannot see that they fail on the same THING. Lens reports now carry a mandatory STRUCTURED TRAILER (FINDING-CLASSES: + ROOT-CAUSE: upstream|drafter); the minter harvests both into the _findings trail; the dispatcher REFUSES round N+1 when two consecutive rounds share a class ("the spec is unsettled, not the prose — escalate to KG") and hard-stops on an upstream diagnosis (pn F13: a reviewer wrote exactly that diagnosis in round 3, in prose nothing acted on, and the loop ran two more wasted rounds). --cap-override with KG's quoted ruling re-opens. Minting untouched — F17's re-dispatch protection is deliberately not weakened.
  • kai-writing: the instrument rule reaches self-review (pn F14). The author's trail was "the least reliable artifact in the loop": three judgement notes ("fixed", "restored") certified fixes the text did not contain, while measured notes were never wrong. record_self_review.py now refuses a judgement-verb note that names no instrument.
  • academic-workflow 1.42.0 (pn F15/F16, twice-reported — a miss on my side): staging paths are exempt from the RECEIPT check only (the gate's own message mandates composing there; lints stay active), and the glossary walk checks each ancestor's paper/ child — it was silently INACTIVE at the mandated staging path, 25 enforced terms checking nothing. Proven live in three probes.

docs.title: 2026-07-21 (later) — Field day 1: the triage PDF learns from KG's live review
docs.text:
• spec-gate 0.10.1 (pn findings F3/F4/F6, KG quoted throughout): an all-unruled page collapses to ONE banner ("I can see a lot of unruled... I'm not sure what I'm supposed to say"); the proposed title prints as a caption stand-in under bare figures; --structure resolves each placement to its owning subsection's title+goal on the page ("I don't see the sections and the section titles"); E-ids print Huge — KG cannot annotate the PDF, so the id is his entire interface; RaggedRight/emergencystretch fix the margin overrun he screenshotted; placeins holds page breaks. 16/16 battery. In-flight uncommitted edits from the field session were verified, tightened (the banner no longer prints over a page with a ruling), covered, shipped — with the reminder that plugin edits belong to the kt session.
  • project-workflow 1.56.2: IDs are PERMANENT doctrine + KG's deliberate appendix ruling (one interpretation line each; does-NOT-show omissible there — the gate already permits this by construction).
  • F1/F2 (migration sequence must build the triage PDF before asking KG anything; migration must HARVEST existing rulings — "re-asking a ruled decision is a migration failure, symmetric with forging one") are answered in coord writing-process-and-gates/010. F7 (runtime version-floor check in reground) queued as a designed item, not rushed.

docs.title: 2026-07-21 — Doc generators read COMMITTED truth, not the workspace (CI red fixed)
docs.text: • The 0df9ac9 push went CI-red on "skill-reference STALE" while local regeneration matched — root cause: the INDEX/skill-reference generators GLOBBED the workspace, so another session's two untracked WIP skill folders inflated the local regeneration to 52 skills against CI's 50-file clean checkout. Both generators now discover via git ls-files (glob fallback only where git is absent): derived docs derive from committed truth, immune to anyone's in-flight work in the shared tree. skill-reference regenerated at 50; verified green WITH the untracked folders still present. The two WIP folders (check-rules, experiment) are another session's and stay untracked — not swept, not deleted.

docs.title: 2026-07-20 (thirteenth) — Coord goes near-push: no more "tell the other session to check"
docs.text: • coord 0.4.0: coord_nudge (UserPromptSubmit). KG's pain: cross-session messages required manually telling the receiving session to check. The honest architecture answer first: TRUE push into an idle session is impossible in any channel — Slack included — because a session executes nothing between turns; and Slack agents are a different runtime without the local project context, hooks, or scripts, while routing coord content through Slack would put strategy-and-deliberation material on an external service. The honest maximum is NEXT-TURN injection, and that is now built: the hook announces NEW inbox messages addressed to this session on its next user turn — inbox-direct (STATE.md can be stale mid-session), once per message (per-session stamp), first run absorbs the backlog silently, own outbound and other sessions' mail never announced, fail-open everywhere. The SessionStart digest remains the backstop. 10/10 battery. En route: release_check caught a version set DOWNWARD (0.3.0 -> "0.2.0" — assumed instead of read) and a stale skill-reference; both fixed pre-push.

docs.title: 2026-07-21 — coord 0.5.0: the standing-watch pattern (no-messenger, layer 3)
docs.text: • coord 0.5.0: the canonical answer to "how do sessions talk without me as messenger" is now doctrine in the SKILL: arm any pinned session once with /loop 25m /coord check. It wakes, handles mail addressed to it, sleeps when the board is quiet. Rules with teeth: idle tick = one STATE.md read (NO subagents — a subagent costs a fresh context, the check is one grep); interval floor 15 min, band 20–30 (mail moves at the user's cadence; each tick is a real turn); lifetime = the session window; quiet board → sleep, never invent work. The confirm-before-write pattern is explicitly waived under a loop mandate — the loop IS the standing authorization for in-remit replies; out-of-remit/destructive/user-addressed items still wait. Composes with the SessionStart digest (0.3.0) and the per-turn near-push nudge (0.4.0) into three delivery layers; with all three, no session needs the user as messenger. (Verification note: the 0.4.0 nudge was briefly mis-diagnosed as unwired this session on a stale Dropbox read — git history settled it; both hook batteries re-run green, 10/10 + 12/12.)

docs.title: 2026-07-20 (twelfth) — The shell route around the prose gate is closed
docs.text: • academic-workflow 1.41.0: guard_bash_prose_write (PreToolUse on Bash). The last proven enforcement hole: the field dry run landed manuscript content through a bash heredoc that the Write tool had just refused — and a strictness with an easy detour trains the detour. The guard denies shell write-intents (redirection, tee, sed -i, cp/mv destination, heredocs, python open(...,'w')) into manuscript prose files (paper/**.tex + clone-root masters). Deliberately narrow: output/ fragments exempt (fragment-from-code is the pattern, not a bypass), .claude/tmp + temp_claude staging exempt, reads/compiles untouched, fail-open on any error. 20/20 battery — 8 bypass forms denied, 11 ordinary-shell forms untouched.

docs.title: 2026-07-20 (eleventh) — The table gate ("tables now") + the last default sets
docs.text:
• academic-workflow 1.40.0: check_table_format.py — KG's table-font discipline mechanized: table sizes are a FIXED set, never a scaling transform's output. RED on \resizebox/\scalebox/adjustbox-width around table content — including the common paper-side \resizebox{...}{\input{tab.tex}} wrap, which a vacuous-pass shortcut initially skipped (the wrapping file has no tabular env; self-review caught it) — on \tiny/\scriptsize inside table scope (floor \footnotesize) and hand-tuned \fontsize. Figure resizebox out of scope (tables only, per KG). Auditable inline waiver. The FAIL routes to build-fragment-table: an overfull table is a DESIGN problem. 13/13 battery.
  • spec-gate 0.10.0: table-format in the registry (able-to-fail verified live) + three more default unit types: table fragments get table-format ALONE; the prose set gains table-format; DELIVERY units get humanize-audit + bib-audit as probes — completing the skill-wiring map from KG's "which other skills should be used here?" question.

docs.title: 2026-07-20 (tenth) — Gates route to skills: the figure gate becomes non-optional; the exhibit template routes to builders
docs.text:
• spec-gate 0.9.0: exhibit-BUILD units (.pdf/.png under output/, or figure-named) receive a figure-review PROBE by default — the review-figure skill's cold-eyes protocol (fresh-context verdict recorded against the artifact hash, auto-staled by edits) stops depending on anyone remembering to run it. The wiring principle of the day, stated: gates route to skills — a deny/probe that names the skill makes probabilistic triggering irrelevant.
  • project-workflow 1.56.1: the EXHIBIT-DECISIONS template gains the skill ROUTING table (KG's question "do we have other skills that should be used here?"): real-data-figure / tikz-figure / simulation-figure / build-fragment-table / build-data-source-table / build-variable-table, each at its exhibit kind — and every exhibit passes review-figure BEFORE Kai's triage, because Kai rules on placement and interpretation; he should never be the one discovering a broken axis.

docs.title: 2026-07-20 (ninth) — KG's closure sweep: dictation receipts, default gate-sets, LaTeX embeds, the cap of 4
docs.text:
• kai-writing: --kg-dictated receipt (KG's ruling: "verbatim only"). When Kai dictates prose in chat, his words ARE the evidence — no agent reviews him. The boundary is mechanical: every final sentence must be his sentence or a ≤3-token edit; ONE session-composed sentence refuses and routes to the four-beat loop, because paraphrase-laundering Kai's words is the exact failure this mode exists to prevent. The dictation is stored beside the final in the receipt.
  • spec-gate 0.8.0: default gate-sets by unit type — corrects the "auto-attached" overstatement (gates attached only when DECLARED; verified at plan_to_conditions.py:369). Prose/.tex units, exhibit-ledger units and plan units now RECEIVE their canonical gates; explicit auditable waiver; every attachment printed; exhibits-first sees bare .tex units.
  • academic-workflow 1.39.0: LaTeX conventions are now CARRIED, not hoped for — latex-fragment-conventions.md is a mandated embed for every kai-writing role and joins check_lens_evidence's mandated set; the prose gate's deny message documents the dictation route.
  • kai-writing: THE CAP (KG: "converge with a cap" of 4). The lens builder reads the unit's _findings trail: dispatching round 4 warns the author in the prompt and on stderr ("if this round does not land it, the next step is KG or a re-plan, not another reviewer"); round 5 REFUSES, with an auditable --cap-override. Suite probes all three branches.
  • Suite hardening en route: the builder battery pins encoding="utf-8" on its subprocess reads — without it, Windows cp1252 killed the reader thread on the first non-cp1252 byte in an embedded rule file and returned stdout=None, which surfaced as a TypeError rather than an encoding error.

docs.title: 2026-07-20 (eighth) — pn's field retrospective encoded: canary, degraded mode, leak-class briefs, instrument rule
docs.text:
• principles/degraded-mode-channels.md (new). pn ran two days with the Bash tool dead: no lints, no receipts, no compiles — "a dead enforcement layer looks exactly like a compliant session" — and lost a day of Stata replications that stata-mcp could run the whole time. The doctrine: bash canary first action (hooks-alive + canary-dead = broken app wrapper), sanctioned degraded-mode fallback (temp_claude staging + per-item DEBT.md + KG sign-off through the full receipt path on recovery), a standing channel inventory, and the instrument rule.
  • spec-gate 0.7.1: the reground SessionStart nudge instructs the canary and routes to the doctrine.
  • kai-writing: pn's two leak-classes are now named hunts in the faithfulness lens — value→category MAPPING (three rounds once checked values while a footnote crossed categories) and citation fidelity against FULL TEXT only (two misattributions survived bib-level review). Every lens verdict now carries the INSTRUMENT RULE: "checked against on "; instrument-less "verified" is void; self-recounting is not an instrument. SKILL.md bans open judgement briefs ("does this cohere?") — pn's most constrained round was the only zero-reject one.

docs.title: 2026-07-20 (seventh) — F3/F4 closed: the fix chain binds to its reviewed root; cross-mode laundering refused
docs.text:
• kai-writing: rewriter chains count novelty against the reviewed ROOT (F3). The 2-novel-sentence allowance used to reset at every hop — each fix's receipt became the next hop's baseline, so three hops smuggled six full novel sentences with zero reviews, all exit 0. --rewriter-only now walks --prior transitively to the nearest non-rewriter receipt (cycle- and broken-chain-guarded) and counts novel sentences against THAT final. Over an author-writes root the allowance is ZERO — its prose was reviewed as it stood, so a novel sentence in a fix round has seen no reviewer at all; new prose goes through the four-beat loop. Word-level fixes stay cheap. meta gains root / root_mode / novel_vs_root.
  • kai-writing: cross-mode re-record REFUSED (F4). A full-mode re-record of a text that already had an author_final receipt overwrote its meta.json, dropped review_sha1s, and freed those reviews for reuse — laundering via the tool's own CLI. _guard_cross_mode now refuses a mode-changing re-record at all three mint sites; superseding a receipt requires deleting it explicitly, a git-visible act. Same-mode re-records unaffected. Suite +3 scenarios incl. a 2-hop chain probe importing final_hash rather than re-deriving it; four-beat integration chain still green.

docs.title: 2026-07-20 (sixth) — L3: the report proves it carried the rules; the codebook rides the conformance lens
docs.text:
• kai-writing: report<->dispatch MANIFEST BINDING at the receipt. The dispatch proved a prompt was BUILT; this closes the stated gap — the review must ECHO the briefing's FILES-MANIFEST, verified against the DISPATCH's file shas (the exact briefing, not today's files). A review with no manifest or a mismatched one is refused with re-run instructions. Cooperative limit stated in-code; the deep current-rules verifier remains check_lens_evidence at the work-unit gate. Compat: minimal/legacy dispatch records without files[] skip the binding.
  • kai-writing: the CONFORMANCE lens now embeds the Lebrun diagnostic-codebook.md (scientific-writing-analysis) as a MANDATED file — KG's hard requirement: reviewers check against the skills, not their memory of them; never-pure-AI-voice is judged against the codebook's diagnostics. Conformance-only (54KB; other lenses stay lean); missing codebook = INACTIVE refusal like any mandated file.
  • academic-workflow 1.38.2: check_lens_evidence verifies EVERY echoed manifest entry (v1 checked only the mandated trio, leaving extra entries decorative); its battery updated to the lens role's real contract (review target + 3 recorded passes) instead of bypassing it. The live four-beat integration chain now also proves: a review without the echoed manifest is refused at minting; the honest echo lands.

docs.title: 2026-07-20 (fifth) — Dispatch provenance closes the receipt's open verdict
docs.text: • kai-writing: --author-final now REQUIRES a lens dispatch hash-bound to the exact text being recorded. Adversarial round 2's standing verdict was that lexical review-binding is cooperative-only (a 148-word generic checklist landed on 11 of 20 paragraphs; the refusal message was a hill-climbable oracle). The durable fix ships: the receipt refuses unless a build_agent_prompt --role lens --review-target dispatch record exists whose review_target_sha1 equals the final file's content hash — proof a reviewer prompt was BUILT for THIS text, with the full rule files embedded. --undispatched-ok "<reason >= 8 words>" is the auditable exception (recorded in meta.json; a short reason is refused). meta gains final_file_sha1 + lens_dispatches + dispatch_waiver. Honest remaining gap, stated in-code: this proves the prompt was built, not that the agent ran — that binding lands with the check_lens_evidence wiring. Suite +3 scenarios; a live FOUR-BEAT integration chain (compose → 3 recorded self-reviews → real builder dispatch → mint) passes end to end, and both skip-a-beat paths refuse. SKILL.md Stage 4 now documents author-writes as the default recording route with the legacy two-drafter path preserved.

docs.title: 2026-07-20 (fourth) — Self-review before any reviewer, hard-gated
docs.text:
• kai-writing: the self-review chokepoint (KG: "hard gates to force it to go at least three times iteratively over its own paragraph"). record_self_review.py records one pass over one artifact (content hash + a >= 8-word note of what the pass checked/changed; "looks good" is refused). build_agent_prompt.py --role lens now REQUIRES --review-target and REFUSES to build until that file has >= 3 recorded passes whose LAST hash matches the file as dispatched — an edit after the final pass stales it. Why: reviewer rounds are expensive and can INJECT error (two live cases in one session); the author iterates cheaply first, and the recorded trail is EMBEDDED in the lens prompt so the reviewer spends its budget on what the author did not already cover. The dispatch record now carries review_target_sha1 — the provenance that this reviewer was briefed on THIS text, which the receipt layer's planned dispatch-provenance check consumes. Legacy roles (critic over agent-made drafts) exempt by design. Battery extended: refusal ladder 0/2 passes, short-note refusal, unlock at 3, trail embedded, stale-hash refusal — it caught a real clobber where the ARTIFACTS block overwrote the REVIEW TARGET line.
  • academic-workflow 1.38.1: the prose-gate deny message is now the FOUR-beat route (compose → self-review x3 recorded → reviewer via the gated builder → mint + land); dropped the stale --round flag from the example (derived from the paper trail since the same-day hardening). SKILL.md documents the chokepoint beside the builder contract.

docs.title: 2026-07-20 (third) — The triage PDF gets a deterministic builder
docs.text: • spec-gate 0.7.0: build_triage_pdf.py. The review artifact the exhibit gate's own FAIL message demands ("present the triage PDF") had NO builder — every session hand-rolled it, and the process dry run's attempt failed to compile. Now deterministic: EXHIBIT-DECISIONS.md rendered one exhibit per page in LEDGER order (deliberately distinct from build_exhibits_preview.py, the after-placement artifact) — E-id header, the exhibit printed as the reader sees it, the decision box with per-field statuses, every PROPOSED field a red UNRULED — needs your verdict flag, ghost blocks a FILE NOT FOUND page, unlisted files a closing page. KG batch-replies by E-id; nothing is reviewable-but-invisible. Output is a generated view under .claude/tmp/ (zero git footprint; deliberately NOT paper/plan/, whose allow-list is closed and whose files would register as unlisted exhibits). Portability finding fixed in the builder itself: Windows 8.3 short names carry ~, an ACTIVE TeX character — pdflatex died under %TEMP%; compiles are now cwd-relative on long-form paths. 13/13 battery incl. a REAL compile of pdf+tex exhibits (the compile probe first false-SKIPPED — bare pdflatex is not on this shell's PATH; the battery now resolves the MiKTeX path); self-view gate on the rendered pages caught a page-1 margin overflow.

docs.title: 2026-07-20 (later) — Pre-writing gates 2/5/6/7 + the remaining templates
docs.text:
• spec-gate 0.6.0: plan-decisions gate. Covers the files the exhibit gate cannot see — the dry run's headline failure was a green stage-1 gate beside 42 unruled decisions in PAPER-STRUCTURE.md and the section plans, plus an exhibit APPROVED into a section KG had deleted. Stage-scoped (2=goals, 5=titles, 6=paragraph counts, 7=leads/cites/how), cumulative ACROSS files so stage 7 also demands a ruled skeleton. INHERITED shows is STRING-MATCHED against the exhibit ledger (a paraphrase between exhibits and prose is the seam that drifted pn's leads); RULED placements must resolve to an existing section block; citing a CUT exhibit fails; DELIVERY enforces citation coverage. Parser imported from check_exhibit_verdicts — one parser, two gates, no dialect drift. Battery 27/27; it caught a real A.1 id-split hole whose field-bleed masked a MAYBE behind a later APPROVED (fixed + first-occurrence-wins fields). Both gates' registry selftests verified able-to-fail live.
  • project-workflow 1.56.0: templates/PAPER-STRUCTURE.md + templates/section_plan.md complete the pre-writing set. Battery-driven template fixes: inherited shows is one line PER cited exhibit; placement format is ASCII main 4.2 (gate tolerates the legacy section sign).

docs.title: 2026-07-20 — Writing-process redesign: author-writes receipts + pre-writing gate 1
docs.text:
• kai-writing: --author-final receipt mode (KG's process inversion, 2026-07-19). The SESSION drafts (it holds the accumulated context); agents only review — sub-agent drafters hallucinated a full validation table in the field. record_pipeline_run.py --author-final --review <R> ... --task "<unit>" records prose against >=1 independent review. Refuses: zero/short reviews, a "review" that is ~the prose (an agent that returns prose is DRAFTING), a review containing a verbatim paste of the final behind filler, duplicate reviews, review reuse across different prose (normalized hashes, per-hash), and section-scale prose behind a paragraph-scale review (derived from the one-review-per-~150-word-paragraph rule). Appends an append-only _findings/<task>.jsonl paper trail, printed at record time so round N+1's reviewer sees rounds 1..N. --round is DERIVED from the trail, not asserted. Two adversarial passes drove the hardening; their verdict stands that binding a review to prose by lexical overlap is cooperative-only — the durable fix (reviewer dispatch provenance) is queued. Committed suite +7 scenarios; 22-probe attack battery green.
  • kai-writing: build_agent_prompt.py fails CLOSED on unknown --lens-name (a typo used to produce a generic "hunt this failure class" reviewer — a verdict with no lens). +2 lens briefs: coherence (cross-paragraph over-polish antidote; judges the RUN, barred from relitigating passed paragraphs) and interpretation (prose vs the AGREED exhibit reading). conformance now names default-AI-voice as the failure class: "clean, competent and anonymous FAILS this lens."
  • academic-workflow 1.38.0: gate_prose_write deny message rewritten to the workable three-beat route (compose in .claude/tmp/sections/ → review → mint receipt → LAND) — the old text was circular (told the author to run a pipeline on text the gate wouldn't let them write). Deny logic unchanged; 6/6 smoke.
  • spec-gate 0.5.0: exhibit-verdicts gate — pre-writing stage 1 (KG: "every exhibit must be approved"). check_exhibit_verdicts.py checks paper/plan/EXHIBIT-DECISIONS.md: REQUIRES the four fields per block with a CLOSED status vocabulary (design principle after v1 shipped nine false-PASS routes: require good text, don't detect bad text), exhibits on disk without a block BLOCK (unlisted), blocks naming missing files BLOCK (ghost), fenced examples stripped, _archive/ skipped, paths resolved not basename-matched. --stage N scopes which decisions must be ruled (a stage-blind gate deadlocked on "titles later" — and a deadlocked gate manufactures forgery); DELIVERY set derived from the stage map (self-review catch: it was laxer than stage 4). Rulings need EVIDENCE: verdict RECORDED + date + quoted words — kills the sed PROPOSED→CHANGED route proven in a full process dry run. 43/43 battery incl. a 9-dialect matrix; registered in GATE_REGISTRY with a known-bad fixture (selftest_expect: 1, able-to-fail verified live).
  • project-workflow 1.55.0: templates/EXHIBIT-DECISIONS.md (ledger template: per-exhibit blocks, shows / does-NOT-show / placement / verdict, pass state, retirement convention that doesn't trip the gate) + canonical-structure.yaml root allows *.bib and NAMED masters (paper.tex/main.tex/ms.tex) — Overleaf compiles root-relative in the clone (KG: work happens in each co-author's clone; container copy is view-only). Narrow on purpose: a stray section/table .tex at root stays denied (suite + probes).
  • Care mode (global): mode_reground.py gains the [care] dimension — KG's importance markers ("be very careful", "think deeply", ...) set a persistent HIGH flag on the work item, released by "care off"; injected every turn beside the mode line. Suite green.
  • Process rule (KG, standing): 2–3 SELF-review iterations before any adversarial dispatch — adversaries are useful but can inject wrong fixes (two live cases this session); self-review of the prewriting spec found 22 defects, 9 of which the process simulation had missed. Log: working/prewriting-stage-spec.md §9.

docs.title: 2026-07-17 — KG planning-doc standardization; the trigger-surface P0 (20 dead descriptions)
docs.text:
• tikz-figure: KNOWN SILENT TRAPS section (pn field report, work-orchestrator thread 019). Four compile-clean-but-look-wrong traps from one real figure: font= REPLACES the picture font (bold labels silently serif — latent in a shipped exhibit); math mode drags serif digits into sans figures; style names shadowing pgf keys (out, in, at, ... — reserved list extended in troubleshooting.md); equal-looking fills with unequal white-text contrast (symmetric in design must be symmetric on the page). Plus: never write .tex through a bash heredoc (swallowed \\ opens display math and eats a tikzpicture). No gate can see these — the skill's defence is the traps list

  • the mandatory render-and-LOOK step.

  • THE TRIGGER-SURFACE P0 (consolidation audit, same-day fix). 20 of 50 SKILL.md frontmatters were UNPARSEABLE YAML — an unquoted description: containing : (colon+space) reads as a nested mapping — so the harness listed those skills with their first BODY line as the description (map-figure/real-data-figure surfaced as "Visual identity — use Kai's theme...", adversarial-review as "<!--card"), or nothing. Verified live via a fresh-context probe agent. Those skills could not semantic-trigger AT ALL — a mechanical root cause under the "sessions ignore the skills" complaint, invisible while everyone tuned description WORDING. Fix: all 20 descriptions quoted (patch bumps: academic-workflow → 1.37.1, r-research-workflow → 1.6.2, talks → 1.8.1; root skills adversarial-review, map-figure, real-data-figure, review-figure). NET: scripts/check_skill_descriptions.py — frontmatter must parse, description non-empty single-line string, WARN over 1500 chars (observed truncation) — wired into release_check.sh (2c). 9 over-length WARNs remain for the description-slimming follow-up. Side effect: the stale ~/.claude/skills/research-presentation shadow was the only PARSEABLE copy of that skill — the canonical talks copy was RED.

  • project-workflow 1.53.0 → 1.54.0 — type set v2 (KG ruling "A", same day, field-calibrated). A read-only scan of all five real paper projects showed: the Miner experiment (the success case) wrote a full paper with ~ZERO planning docs (conversation + direct .tex); the most-updated planning doc anywhere is pn's exhibit decisions ledger (11 commits); no project ever kept section structure + plan as two living files; .md prose drafts (id-mining, 75KB abstract_drafts.md) produced merge maps and double maintenance. v2 therefore: + EXHIBIT-DECISIONS.md (append-only exhibit rulings ledger), − <section>_structure.md (structure/leads live INSIDE <section>_plan.md; kai-writing's Kai-facing doc IS the plan file), and the anti-rule prose is never drafted as .md (deny redirects to kai-writing). Battery extended (intro_structure.md and intro_draft.md now DENY). Coord thread planning-doc-field-evidence asks pn/uam/id-mining for judgment; amendments stay one-line manifest edits.
  • project-workflow 1.52.0 → 1.53.0 — KG's planning-doc standardization (ruling 2026-07-17). paper/plan/ is THE planning home, git-tracked, STRICT typed set enforced by the structure gate (superseded same day by v2 above) — anything else in there is denied with redirects. temp_claude/ is canonical for working DOCUMENTS & scratch (SUPERSEDES the 2026-07-02 .claude/tmp decision; .claude/tmp/ stays as machine temp for tools; .claude/plans/ → .claude/plan/, reserved for non-paper /work plans). Canonical doc gains the "Planning documents & where .md files live" section (the four-homes rule: paper/plan | temp_claude | project_management | .claude machine state); manifest, gate battery (8 new scenarios), guard_clutter wording, bootstrap-project scaffold + README table + gitignore, templates (per-clone scratch → clone_<XX>/temp_claude/), kai-writing SKILL (paper/.plan → paper/plan/), /work SKILL + plan-template (paper plans → paper/plan/), stage-boundary design v3.1 all aligned. Mirror re-synced; INDEX regenerated.

docs.title: 2026-07-15 — academic-workflow 1.25.0: the writing deny-gate; spec-gate GATE_REGISTRY Class 1
docs.text:
• academic-workflow 1.24.2 → 1.25.0. First hooks in this plugin: gate_prose_write.py (PreToolUse on Write|Edit|MultiEdit) DENIES writing manuscript .tex text that violates Kai's hard prose rules — check_voice (banned words/phrases, dash+colon limits, transition chains) + check_glossary (banned terms, only when the paper has a CONCEPTS.md). Diff-scoped by construction: only the incoming new_string/content is linted — existing file text, co-author prose, and quotes are never examined, and nothing is ever written into the LaTeX file (Kai's design decisions, 2026-07-15). Exempt: exhibits/, tikz_*/tab_*, preambles, templates, fixtures, slides/lectures/talks trees. Fail-open on every error; 8-scenario able-to-fail battery (hooks/test_gate_prose_write.py), including the diff-scope guarantee (violation only in old_string → allowed).
  • spec-gate: GATE_REGISTRY Class 1 wired. plan_to_conditions.py now registers banned-phrases → check_voice and glossary-terms → check_glossary with known-bad fixtures, so plan-driven runs (plan_verify) execute them mechanically. Selftest hardening found by the battery: passing selftests were silent (indistinguishable from none — now surfaced), and any non-zero exit falsely confirmed able-to-fail (a broken fixture path exits 2 and would pass — new selftest_expect pins the exact failure code).
  • PROTECTED.md edit-protection (Kai's design, same day). The hook's second duty, the SHIELD: text listed in a paper's PROTECTED.md (content-anchored entries — anchor + scope exact|paragraph|section + reason; never line numbers, never anything in the .tex) cannot be edited by an agent at all until Kai lifts the entry — the "no autonomous rewrites" rule mechanized. Deny names the entry + reason; whole-file Writes must keep the span verbatim; a structurally broken PROTECTED.md fails CLOSED (a shield that silently fails open is no shield); stale anchors protect nothing (documented limit). Template: templates/PROTECTED.md. Battery now 14 scenarios (shield: deny-inside / allow-outside / Write-drop denied / Write-verbatim allowed / stale-anchor / broken-file).
  • Same lint engine, two triggers: the hook nets everyday unplanned edits; plan gates own planned artifacts (lead-orchestrator arc, tasks #59/#60).
  • RECEIPT MATCHER V2 — sentence-level coverage (academic-workflow → 1.30.0; the top daily-friction item from both field testers). v1's whole-text containment wrongly rejected valid receipts on mixed edits (pn: prose interleaved with headers/placeholder comments, receipts 842da503/3190d195; uam: context lines around receipted prose — ~3–4 wasted round-trips each). v2 judges coverage per SENTENCE: every produced sentence must appear in a receipt's final.txt — with three principled exemptions: word-level edits (≤3-token symmetric diff; closes uam's deleted-"on"-blocked vs word-swap-passed inconsistency), text ported verbatim from git-TRACKED repo .tex (co-author provenance; matched via normalized sentence sets, not line-based grep — .tex sentences wrap), and comments/headers/context which are simply never "produced". Able-to-fail preserved and sharpened: a novel unreceipted sentence still blocks, and the deny now NAMES it.
  • CHAT GATE — detector + matcher brought to parity (academic-workflow → 1.30.1, 1.30.2). 1.30.1: short bare LEADS detected — uam's field report showed the ONE un-piped text that reached Kai was a lead sentence in plain chat (too short for the fenced/60-word signals); an explicit lead-marker line (Lead:, Proposed sentence:) with a real prose payload now blocks, while feedback ABOUT a lead never matches. 1.30.2 (pn field report 006): the chat gate's receipt lookup still used v1 whole-text containment, so quoting a RECEIPTED sentence inside a longer message — which /work Step 2.2 MANDATES when Kai asks for the plan in chat — false-positived (fragment neither contains nor is contained by the receipt's final.txt). Two of our own rules colliding. Fix: the chat gate now IMPORTS the write gate's matcher v2 (sentence-level coverage + tracked-.tex exemption; one matcher, never re-derived). Battery proves both directions: a receipted sentence wrapped in ledger labels passes (RED pre-fix with exactly pn's deny message), and a novel sentence in the same block still blocks.
  • INACTIVE — a distinct gate verdict + the walk-up audit (spec-gate → 0.3.0, academic-workflow → 1.31.0; pn's asks b + c from field report 004). (b) A checker that exits 2 with the word INACTIVE (ran, but cannot see its config) now surfaces in spec_gate as its own INACT verdict with wiring guidance — still a hard build-stop, but never again a red-among-reds: pn's 9 identical "glossary REDs" trained the operator to treat the gate as noise, the exact failure spec-gate exists to prevent. Exit 2 WITHOUT the word stays plain RED (argparse/infra errors must not masquerade). (c) Audit of every registry checker for walk-up-from-artifact config discovery: check_voice / check_para_length (pure lints) and check_claim_strength (explicit --ack-dir) are clean; check_glossary + check_number_trace were already fixed at emit; check_exhibit_refs had a live instance — its 3-parent master discovery cannot find paper/*.tex from a .claude/tmp/ artifact (sibling subtree), silently degrading to fragment-alone analysis (false REDs for exhibits referenced from OTHER sections). Fixed with a new --master flag + emit-time {master_flag} resolution; on an out-of-closure draft the checker analyzes the master+draft UNION (the post-merge question — master-alone would false-GREEN by ignoring the draft entirely); a missing declared master is INACTIVE, not a content verdict. Batteries: spec-gate 39/39 (INACT label + hard stop + no-masquerade), exhibit-refs 10 scenarios (union pass + fragment-alone control RED + draft-orphan still blocks + missing-master INACTIVE), plan_to_conditions S6 (emitted --master fires both ways).
  • STRUCTURE GATE: push-time audit + housekeeping net (project-workflow -> 1.50.0; uam asks 5.4 + 5.5 -- the last two items from the canonical-structure package). gate_structure.py --audit --project <root> [--tracked] runs the write-hook's OWN evaluate() over existing paths (git-tracked +/- untracked; bounded walk without git), so the three enforcement moments can never drift: write-time deny (primary), push-time audit over the tracked tree (5.4 -- the last defense before a violation ships as co-author-visible, Overleaf-synced precedent), and housekeeping Check 10 (structure-manifest) at SessionStart (5.5 -- the net for rot that PREDATES any gate, the figures_all/ class; research-mode projects only, MED severity, explicitly not the primary control). Push-time step documented in the canonical-structure rule (both copies). Battery extended: seeded pre-existing rot named + exit 1, clean tree exit 0, non-research project says not-applicable; Check 10 smoke-verified on a live fixture; multiclone battery 8/8 regression-green.
  • TALK-FIRST MODE (KG decision, 2026-07-16; Claude-Code-only by construction). Two pieces against agents running off mid-discussion (KG: "it's not good when we're still in the discussion stage... when there's a clear goal, work until the goal"). Piece 1: the INTERACTION MODE rule at the top of the global CLAUDE.md -- discussion is the default; execution is ENTERED on an explicit go-signal, never inferred; a decision announced in conversation is INPUT, not a work order; "hold on" drops back mid-execution. Piece 2 (this repo): scripts/mode_reground.py, a UserPromptSubmit hook injecting the CURRENT mode into EVERY turn (per-session state; deterministic exact-token flips -- bare "go" / "go: " / /work / a /loop mandate; "hold on" / "let's discuss" / "stop" drop back) -- the reground pattern, so the contract cannot decay out of context in long sessions (the word "go" inside a sentence never flips; battery-proven, 9 scenarios). Registered in the user settings.json; deployed to ~/.claude/hooks/. Piece 3 (an ask-tier PreToolUse guard in discuss mode) deliberately HELD until field data shows 1+2 leak.
  • THE TITLE REGISTER (writing_style_kai.md 3b; talks -> 1.8.0; KG ruling 2026-07-16, pn 018). Narrative/assertion titles were hard-coded as doctrine in four skills and gated per-slide -- KG rejected them for research artifacts ("I don't want these narrative titles in research papers or presentations... in a blog post that is fine"), and every agent-proposed section title in the populism paper asserted while every KG-supplied title was descriptive. The preference now lives ONCE, as a per-genre register in his profile: paper main sections = canonical set, never narrative; paper subsections = descriptive default, narrative a rare proposed option; research decks = structural slides keep canonical titles ("they just have to be there"), assertion titles occasional and NEVER a per-slide requirement; teaching lectures unchanged (OWID narrative doctrine deliberate); blogs/non-research free. Enforcement aligned: title_lint's label-title check FAIL -> WARN (number-dumps stay fatal), the talks slide-reviewer checks an assertion title's truth when present instead of requiring one, real-data-figure's description genre-scopes its narrative-title doctrine. The two lecture-pipeline-owned skills (comparative-statics-figure, lecture-feedback) are handed to lp by coord -- teaching keeps narrative titles, so their substance stands. Batteries: title_lint 17/17 (3 scenarios rewritten to the register contract), stage/slide gates green.
  • EXHIBITS NAMING ENFORCED + THE INLINE-TIKZ RULING (project-workflow -> 1.52.0; uam Q1/Q2, KG ruling 2026-07-16). The structure manifest now enforces the type prefix inside exhibits/ (tikz_.tex / tab_.tex) -- the spec stated it, the gate allowed .tex, and uam proved the naming rule was documentation-only by violating it while building the folder. And the canonical rule gains KG's ruling: exhibit figure source is STANDALONE and builds to output/figures/.pdf, because inline-input TikZ produces no output file and is therefore INVISIBLE to the figure colour gates (4 UAM figures in the paper + 3 decks escaped gating by construction). Battery +4 scenarios.
  • NEW SKILL /build-variable-table (academic-workflow -> 1.37.0; id-mining ask 4). Codebook -> LaTeX variable-definitions appendix table, grouped by family -- the shape two projects (miner paper, UAM's submod_vardefs.tex) independently hand-authored. The CODEBOOK is the source of truth (canonical home data/documentation/codebook.md; known legacy spots checked): family headings + markdown tables with Variable + Definition; optional Source/Submodule/Scale/Construction/Valid-for columns are ADAPTIVE (appear only when populated -- the primary-data lesson applied from day one); the load-bearing Valid-for column (which contrasts a variable is valid for) is first-class. A prose-only codebook exits 1 with a convert-the-codebook-FIRST instruction (with the user, never silently) -- the conversion is the durable improvement, the table falls out. [H] float per rule 8 v2, texttt variables, family multicolumn headers, provenance comment. Smoke: adaptive columns, escaping, family subset, unknown-family named, prose-only refusal.
  • CONTAINER GUARD: findings now AGE (project-workflow -> 1.51.0; uam's ratchet fix, seconded by pn). "It reports, it does not converge -- being told twice does nothing for the third time." The SessionStart hygiene advisory now carries per-finding age from a .scratch-state.json sidecar at the container root (Dropbox-synced, so counts aggregate): "output/ (first seen 2026-06-17, still present after 9 sessions)" -- a debt with a number. Sessions increment once per SessionStart only (direct CLI runs read without counting); resolved findings are PRUNED so a recurrence starts fresh; read-only containers degrade gracefully to the plain report. Deliberately NOT built: --fix (an auto-mover at a shared container root is where a helper can eat uncommitted work). uam's .scratch-allow justification is now the docstring's usage guidance verbatim ("silencing would be lying to ourselves"). Battery 56/56 incl. the aging arc (no note on first sighting -> counted on second -> direct-run no-increment -> pruned on resolution).
  • find_work bystander filter (first live defect, same day). A thread between two OTHER sessions surfaced as kt work because any non-self message counted. A thread is OURS only if the session ever wrote in it or a message's to: names it; battery scenario proves bystander-silent + addressed-to-surfaces. Live scan: 4 items -> 2 real.
  • FIND_WORK -- the finds-the-work loop block (kt #79; loop-engineering map). scripts/find_work.py --session <name> makes autonomous-loop work discovery DETERMINISTIC: P0 failing release-check on origin (responder contract), P1 coord threads with unanswered inbound messages (needs: execution > feedback > none; mtime-based -- a fresh reply silences a thread, a newer inbound re-surfaces it), exit 3 = fall back to the internal task queue then a long heartbeat. The session EXECUTES the top item instead of judging what matters -- the same in-model-judgment failure class as skill triggering, one level up. Proof on first live run: it surfaced a needs-execution thread whose WORK had shipped hours earlier but whose in-thread reply was forgotten -- exactly the miss the scanner exists to catch. 5-scenario hermetic battery + live-scan smoke.
  • DATA-SOURCE TABLE FITS PRIMARY-DATA PAPERS (academic-workflow -> 1.36.1; id-mining field report). build_table.py columns are now ADAPTIVE: Source/URL appear only when at least one dataset populates them (a LaTeX comment names what was omitted and why) -- the fixed shape printed two blank columns on every row of an own-data paper and was unusable in the field. New optional per-dataset provenance: (primary | administrative | third-party) and coverage: fields surface as columns when populated -- the shape id-mining hand-authored, generalized. Float spec fixed [htbp] -> [H] per rule 8 v2. The canonical datasets: field list is now documented in the skill (it was discoverable only by grepping the helper; two projects drifted), and /build-variable-table is named as the planned companion (two projects independently hand-built that exact shape). Smoke-tested both shapes.
  • oTREE TRILOGY INTEGRATED (experiment-methods -> 0.8.0; Andrea's PR #2, KG decision A). Andrea Mentasti's three oTree skills moved (git mv, authorship preserved) from top-level skills/ into the experiment-methods plugin -- the lifecycle is now complete in one installable unit: design -> pre-register -> ethics -> BUILD (otree-build-app) -> PREFLIGHT (otree-preflight) -> DEPLOY (otree-deploy). Kept as three skills deliberately: three workflow moments with disjoint trigger vocabularies (authoring / pre-launch gating / ops), and preflight stays a read-only maker-checker firewall -- merging would dilute triggering and violate the adversarial doctrine. Additive cross-wiring only (Andrea's content untouched): build-app states its pipeline position (implement design_spec.yaml, never re-derive the design), preflight gains pre-registration-consistency review scope + the canonical doctrine posture, experiment-design's hand-off now names the implementation arm. Quality note: the trilogy independently arrived at our adversarial recipe (find-not-reassure, graded verdicts, read-only reviewer) -- a strong drop.
  • FLOAT RULE v2 + THE WRITING RUNBOOK (academic-workflow -> 1.36.0; the own-goal fixed and KG's help-first directive). latex-fragment-conventions rule 8 redesigned SCALE-AWARE: v1's "default to [H]" caused the field disease it now documents -- [H] on all 80 floats ejects pages (systematic half-empty pages) and SILENTLY DISABLES placeins/\FloatBarrier (a barrier cannot restrain a float that never floats; KG's eleven barriers were no-ops). v2: [H] only for isolated placement-critical exhibits in prose-dominant text; [h!]/[!htbp] under [section]{placeins} for figures and float-heavy work (barriers BIND there); [p] float pages acceptable in pure-exhibit appendices; never blanket-[H] -- the sparse-page gate is the tripwire, and the fix is the spec, never more barriers. KG's paramount law (exhibit stays in its section) unchanged. And kai-writing ships RUNBOOK.md: the one-page HAPPY PATH (plan shape with exhibits-first, builder -> drafters -> critic -> rewriter -> receipt -> lenses -> evidence check, the fix-round line, the document-as-document delivery pass, the ops traps that each cost a real session) -- the gates tell sessions when they are wrong; the runbook tells them how to be right. Linked as START HERE from the skill.
  • LAYOUT ASSERTIONS + EXHIBITS-FIRST AS A PLAN PROPERTY (academic-workflow -> 1.35.0, spec-gate -> 0.4.0; pn's layout post-mortem closed). check_pdf_structure.py gains the checks that "76 pages, zero errors, clean" could never make: (5) SPARSE PAGES -- per-page fill ratio flags half-empty pages (the [H]-ejection shape), page numbers listed, docs under 6 pages exempt; (6) ORPHANED PRINTED FLOATS -- every printed "Figure N:"/"Table N:" caption whose number never appears in body text (roman numerals handled, arabic ranges "Figures 2--4" expanded), the PDF-level twin of label-resolution -- 17 of these shipped while every \label resolved; (7) --render-pages DIR renders every page to PNG: the material for the DOCUMENT-AS-DOCUMENT pass (read the compiled artifact as a reader; at least one adversarial lens gets pages, never prose). And the plan emitter now REFUSES the plan shape that caused it all: >= 2 prose units with no exhibit-inventory unit BEFORE the first one is BLOCKED at emit time (pn's exact ordering -- exhibit unit scheduled last -- is a battery scenario), with an explicit auditable waiver (exhibits_first: waived (<reason>)) for genuinely exhibit-free work. A transmitted rule does not survive plan authoring; only a mechanism does. Batteries: pdf-structure 11 scenarios, plan_to_conditions S7 (refuse / pn-ordering refuse / inventory-first pass / waiver pass).
  • RECEIPT PROVENANCE V2 + THE LENS EVIDENCE GATE (kai-writing recorder v2, academic-workflow -> 1.34.0) -- pn's 012 closed end to end. The recorder now refuses what pn gamed in good faith: (1) SAME-SKELETON pairs -- v1's word-set Jaccard passed their fabricated four-words-apart pair at 0.786; v2 adds a sequence-ratio guard (>=0.85 = one draft, twice) and the battery's scenario 1 IS their pair; (2) STALE-DRAFT LAUNDERING -- recording a materially new final against drafts that already back a receipt is refused, naming the prior and pointing at the honest path; (3) the honest path exists: --rewriter-only --prior <hash> --finding "<lens finding>" records a fix round as what it is -- a rewriter pass over a named receipt -- and mechanically refuses smuggled novel prose (>2 novel sentences; <=2 warn as likely splits/merges). The FIX-ROUND LINE pn asked for is stated in kai-writing Stage 4: a fix round may EDIT existing sentences; a NEW sentence needs a drafter pair, even inside a fix round. (4) DISPATCH PROVENANCE: receipts link to the builder's dispatch records (--task auto-match) -- provenance: dispatched proves two agents were briefed; absent records warn loudly as unverified. And the net: check_lens_evidence.py VOIDS any lens report without a valid, CURRENT FILES-MANIFEST (missing mandated file named; stale sha1 = briefed on superseded rules = re-run) -- wired into /work step 4 so a verdict only counts after its evidence passes. Batteries: recorder 7 scenarios, evidence gate 6 (the valid case harvests the manifest from the REAL builder), write/chat-gate regressions green.
  • THE PROMPT-BUILDER -- constructive dispatch for writing agents (kai-writing; KG's Option C, the keystone). build_agent_prompt.py generates every drafter/critic/ rewriter/lens prompt FROM the rule files: academic-writing.md EMBEDDED first (precedence), profile, exemplars, the paper's CONCEPTS.md -- full content, not paths-to-read (instructions to read are skippable; embedded text is not), with a verifiable FILES-MANIFEST (sha1+mtime) the agent must echo as its report header. Drafter A/B get differentiated angles (claim-first vs evidence-first -- real competition by construction); critic/lens prompts carry the adversarial doctrine baked in (German calibration anchors, refute-by-default, minimum-findings, named failure-mode lens, missing-artifact honesty). Every build writes a DISPATCH RECORD (.claude/pipeline_runs/_dispatch/) -- role, prompt hash, files manifest, timestamps -- the provenance receipts will link to (kt #76). A missing mandated rule file REFUSES (exit 2 INACTIVE): the builder never emits an under-briefed agent, because a badly-briefed adversarial agent converts uncertainty into false certainty. kai-writing Stage 1 + /work step 4 now mandate the builder; hand-composed prompts are banned with the pn 012/013 evidence cited inline. 5-scenario battery (embedding proven by distinctive-line grep from the REAL files, precedence order, A/B hash difference, doctrine elements, refusal path).
  • BUILD-OUTPUT STRUCTURAL CHECK (academic-workflow -> 1.33.0; id-mining Ask 1). check_pdf_structure.py asserts the COMPILED PDF's structure -- the class of failure a spec cannot catch (the structure was authored correctly, then a SUPERSEDED comment block silently swallowed \printbibliography + the whole appendix; compiled cleanly, shipped 9 days with no bibliography until KG read the PDF). Four assertions: (1) a References/Bibliography heading with real entry text renders; (2) zero ?? marks in the rendered text + zero undefined warnings in the .log (the tripwire that was never checked); (3) if the SOURCE declares an appendix, the PDF must show an appendix start -- the assertion that would have fired; (4) page-count delta vs the last build surfaced loudly (sidecar state), warn-only by default, --max-page-delta N makes big swings fatal. Hermetic 7-scenario battery (the incident itself is scenario 1); wired into latex-local-build rule step 5 as the mechanized form of "verify like a build system". Ask 2 (retire the inline SUPERSEDED-block convention) was already codified in coding-workflow.md; this check is the mechanical backstop that rule promises.
  • EXHIBIT-VERIFICATION SUITE (academic-workflow -> 1.32.0, spec-gate -> 0.3.1; pn's 005 asks a-e, all shipped). KG doctrine mechanized: the RENDERED exhibit is the authority, the fragment is an input to it -- pn documented five failure classes from one section, all invisible in the .tex (dropped observations revealed only by a companion table; design facts living in float notes; a caption contradicting its rows; printed numbers != placeholder numbers; column heads that exist only in the wrapper). New: (c) the label-resolution plan gate -- check_label_refs.py blocks any ef/utoref in produced prose whose \label exists nowhere in the manuscript (master UNION draft), with did-you-mean suggestions; pn's two dead labels are the reference case. Registry entry with {master_flag} emit-time wiring + known-bad fixture. (d) render_float.py -- reads the .aux, finds the page carrying a label, renders it to PNG (PyMuPDF), reports the PRINTED number; --list enumerates; stale-.aux and missing-.aux fail honestly. (a+b+e) SKILL.md exhibit-verification step before results prose (render + read + record printed facts into the brief + cite column/row/panel + TWO-checker rule: assembler AND an independent faithfulness agent recomputing against the rendered page) + full SS-A.16 doctrine next to A.13. Batteries: label-refs 6 scenarios (incl. fragment-alone control
  • INACTIVE), render-float 5 (hermetic -- fitz-built PDF + hand-written .aux), S6 extended (label-resolution RED on a dead ref while exhibit-refs stays GREEN -- clean separation).
  • kai-writing: A.15 design-doc currency + field-residue notes (from pn 003 + uam 002). New §A.15 in section-architecture.md (+ Stage-B precondition in SKILL.md): for EXPERIMENTAL sections, cross-check the newest design doc against the FIELDED materials BEFORE leads are drafted — fielded materials win on conflict. pn's live failure: a Stage-B-approved lead described a superseded design ("three attributed texts") and died in verification only after Kai had signed it off; the check belongs before the sign-off. Ops notes added to Stage 4: never author helper .py/.tex via bash heredocs (one backslash level eaten even single-quoted — Write tool then run); the 200-word-cap vs citation-transparency tension documented as a conscious trade (compress citation detail, never silently de-cite, prefer splitting). check_voice lexicon carries uam's citekey insurance note (banned words inside \cite*{} keys must never fire — verified both directions). Coord CONVENTIONS.md gains the NNN-collision rule (concurrent same-prefix messages are siblings; never renumber; next writer takes max+1; cite collided messages by full filename).
  • THE FILE-LINK GATE — no dead link ever reaches Kai again (project-workflow → 1.49.0; universal tier). KG's longest-recurring complaint, mechanized: "I keep repeating this in every session, and then it gets fixed in the session — it should be fixed universally." A Stop hook blocks any reply carrying a file link that does not resolve from the session cwd, or an absolute/file:// href (never clickable, verified repeatedly) — and where the target is findable, the gate COMPUTES the correct cwd-relative href and offers it verbatim (the miscounted-../ case, KG's actual failure, is battery scenario 1). URLs, anchors, and fenced example links pass; loop-guarded; fail-open. Universal-tier blocking is justified under the two-tier doctrine because link resolution is objective — near-zero false positives.
  • Canonical doc: three KG design facts codified (via uam 004). (1) Dropbox-first, GitHub-second: a gitignored destination is a legitimate resting place — every co-author syncs Dropbox; the one real boundary is a GitHub-only clone outside Dropbox. (2) All decks → paper/presentations/ with the \graphicspath ../-depth fix — supersedes the 2026-07-07 revert. (3) Serialize structure-touching work: the misfiling incident arose under workstream concurrency; moves/new-folders/reorganizing pushes are serialized, never interleaved.
  • THE TWO-TIER DOCTRINE — gate scoping from first principles (Kai, 2026-07-16; project-workflow → 1.48.1, academic-workflow → 1.29.2). Kai's design review of the structure gate produced the general scoping rule for ALL enforcement: universal tier (wrong everywhere: version-suffix copies, raw-data overwrites, container escapes) = the ask-tier guards that run in every session; research tier (the pipeline's canon: the structure deny-gate, prose gates, receipts, plan gates) = fires ONLY in research-labeled projects. Rationale: a domain spec enforced outside its domain produces false denies, and false denies teach agents to argue with or evade gates — poisoning them where they're right. Concretely: the structure gate now keys on housekeeping's detect_project_mode (the ## Project mode declaration in project CLAUDE.md wins; structural fallback needs STRONG paper signals — a lone code/ or data/ folder never gates a project); the chat-prose gate requires a paper/ dir with .tex, never a bare root *.tex (the lecture workspace was leaking in). Also closed in the same review: the self-exemption hole — the gated agent could write its own .claude/structure.yaml override in one tool call; that file is now Kai-authored by decree (the gate denies agent writes to it). Batteries extended: undeclared code/+data project silent, course-pipeline workspace silent, undeclared strong-signal paper still gated, self-exemption denied, lecture-root .tex silent.
  • THE STRUCTURE GATE — write-time canonical-structure enforcement (project-workflow → 1.48.0; uam field report, the cleanest evidence yet). In one session six mechanical gates caught the same agent every time; the folder-structure rule — in context on every turn — was violated silently (4 misfiled files + an invented folder, pushed to main, synced toward Overleaf). "I did not forget; I never asked. A tree diagram does not return an exit code." Now: the canonical structure is machine-readable (structure/canonical-structure.yaml — the spec becomes the enforced thing), and gate_structure.py (PreToolUse deny) resolves every Write/Edit target against it and denies with the canonical destination named. New directories require Kai's approval (an invented folder is permanent — every later session treats it as precedent, exactly how figures_all/ became the sole home of 84 files). Kai's call: enforced by default on every research-shaped project (silent on infra/scratch), overridable wholesale via .claude/structure.yaml. Battery drives uam's actual failures.
  • No inline "superseded block" in manuscripts (coding-workflow.md; id-mining field report). A bulk-commented block of dead prose IS a version suffix living in the live file — it cost a paper its entire bibliography for 9 days when a % SUPERSEDED block ran past its end and silently commented out 67 lines of structural machinery (\printbibliography, \appendix, the A-lettering). Rule: superseded prose is DELETED (git carries history); never bulk-comment a block inline; if unavoidable, dead prose ONLY (never \printbibliography/\appendix/ counters) and verify the END marker sits at the true end. The build-output check (queued) is the mechanical backstop.
  • Three gate defects the field found in last night's gates (academic-workflow → 1.29.1): check_para_length under-counted sentences (bare-endswith abbreviation guard ate real boundaries — "included."→"ed"; 9-sentence paragraphs passed); the receipt gate blocked the % PIPELINE NOTE: comment kai-writing mandates (comments now stripped first); and check_glossary could print OK while enforcing junk header terms (a subagent's explanatory table hijacked the parser — it now requires a header carrying both "canonical" and "banned", never breaks on the wrong table, and reports INACTIVE naming the cause). All regression-locked.
  • Field-test round 1 — fixes from uam + pn running the gates on real writing (2026-07-15/16). Kai's design call: the live sessions doing real work ARE the validation, not a staged demo. Day-one verdict: the system carried real writing (pn: a full 7-paragraph section, every sentence drafters → critic → gates → receipt → compile; uam: 6 blocks, 6 true positives, zero false positives) and the lenses caught substance no lexicon could (a mislabeled FE, an accounting identity misread as a finding, a claim false on the paper's own data). Fixes:
  • Emit-time config resolution (spec-gate → 0.2.2). pn found the first silently permissive defect: the glossary plan-gate relied on walk-up discovery from the artifact; plan artifacts live in .claude/tmp/ whose ancestors never hold paper/CONCEPTS.md, so the terminology gate had never fired and its permanent RED read as noise ("a check nobody believes is a check nobody reads"). plan_to_conditions.py now bakes --glossary/--numbers in at emit time (number-trace shared the root cause); battery scenario S5 reproduces the geometry and asserts RED-via-exit-1 (fired), not exit-2 (inactive).
  • Connector-colon budget → per-paragraph ≤1 (Kai's call). The per-unit cap (≤2/file) collided with Kai-approved colon-carrying leads — a long section was over budget by construction and the voice gate force-amended stage-gated leads (two mechanisms disagreeing about authority). Per-paragraph targets the real tell (colon-stacking in one paragraph); approved leads across paragraphs pass by construction. 18/18 smoke cases.
  • Queued from the reports: receipt matcher v2 (both testers hit whole-text containment), chat-gate short-lead detection (uam documented an un-piped lead reaching Kai through chat — the exact failure the build targets), INACTIVE as a verdict distinct from RED, and pn's design-doc-currency Stage-B check (an approved lead was wrong because drafted from a superseded design doc — the exhibits-first analog, found live).
  • Compound-engineering adoption — two mechanisms, no install (Kai's decision after the EveryInc/compound-engineering-plugin evaluation: heavy overlap with our stack, theirs prose-tier, ours gate-tier; steal the residue). (1) /work Step 5 — Compound: a mandatory closing beat routing what the task taught to its one home — Kai corrections → doctrine (propose, he canonizes); gate false positives → calibration input with exact text; revealed preferences → memory; process friction → task/coord. Nothing-found is a valid outcome. (2) housekeeping Check 9 — memory refresh (project-workflow → 1.47.0): every concrete machine path a project memory names must still exist — catches learnings that rotted and mislead with confidence. Calibrated on its own first live run (31 hits → 28 false positives → matcher tightened → 2 genuine findings, both the dead pre-consolidation Dropbox\GitHub\ path, fixed on the spot); synthetic able-to-fail proven.
  • Number-trace — Class-2 checker #4, the last (academic-workflow → 1.29.0; Kai's call: generated numbers.json). The lp locked-number pattern ported to papers. build_numbers_json.py generates paper/numbers.json from the machine outputs that already exist (data/processed/fit_*_tidy.csv), with a curated derived section for prose-computed quantities (each citing its inputs) that survives regeneration. check_number_trace.py requires every prose numeral to trace to it — rounding-tolerant, sign-agnostic, percent/proportion-scaled; curated skips (years, counts < 13, structural refs, float-env numbers) documented and extendable only with sign-off; missing lock = fail-closed RED naming the generator. Master-resolved like exhibit-refs; plan/delivery gate only (mid-draft prose legitimately precedes lockdown). 6-scenario battery; all nine toolkit batteries green. GATE_REGISTRY now carries all six writing gates: banned-phrases · glossary-terms · exhibit-refs · para-length · claim-strength · number-trace.
  • Pipeline receipts + the chat-delivery gate (academic-workflow → 1.28.0; Kai's complaint: "agents give me proposals that were not checked, not in my style, not iterated"). Two mechanisms close the last ungated channels. (1) Receipts: kai-writing's Stage 4 records its real artifacts (Draft A ≠ Draft B, critic report, final text) via record_pipeline_run.py into .claude/pipeline_runs/<hash>/; the write-hook DENIES sentence-level produced prose (the delta vs what it replaces — pre-existing text carried by a Write is exempt; word-level fixes exempt; Kai's scope: even one sentence counts) without a matching receipt. Honesty checks refuse fake receipts (near-identical drafts, trivial critic). (2) Chat gate: a Stop hook in paper projects blocks ending the turn when the reply contains an inline draft- prose block (LaTeX markers or proposal-marker + long prose) with no receipt — chat carries structure documents and pointers, never unchecked proposals. Feedback on Kai's own text is untouched by construction (writes no files, proposes no draft). 8 batteries green, incl. the full receipt round-trip (deny → record real artifacts → same edit passes) and the loop guard.
  • check_claim_strength.py — Class-2 checker #3 (academic-workflow → 1.27.0; Kai's call: BLOCK with an ask-Kai path). The §9 invariant mechanized: a revision must not silently recalibrate epistemic strength in either direction. Blocks on the swap signature (hedge removed + strong added: suggests→shows) or an in-place de-hedge/re-hedge of the SAME claim (>50% token overlap: "may be"→"is"); legitimately new or deleted content passes (low overlap, no swap). The ask-Kai path is mechanical and ONE-SHOT: after Kai's explicit yes in chat, --approve records the exact old/new pair hash in the project's .claude/; the retry passes once and the entry is consumed. Wired three ways: write-hook (Edit's old_string/new_string IS the original-revision pair — the deny carries the exact approve command), plan gate (--git-baseline: artifact vs git HEAD; no baseline = new content = pass), 9-scenario battery (both directions, both protections, one-shot approval proven).
  • check_para_length.py — Class-2 checker #2 (academic-workflow → 1.26.0). Kai's paragraph rule mechanized: 4–6 sentences and ≤200 words per prose paragraph, ≤2 short exceptions per paper (the third is RED). LaTeX-aware by curation, not pretense: protected abbreviation list (e.g./et al./Fig./decimals/initials/U.S.), floats/lists/math/preamble/colon-intros excluded. Registered as the para-length plan gate (full mode) AND wired into the write-hook in --max-only mode — over-length is checked at the keystroke, under-length only on the finished artifact (a partial edit legitimately writes a short fragment). 8-scenario battery; hook battery extended to 16.
  • check_exhibit_refs.py — first Class-2 checker (A.13 mechanized). Every float-environment label (figures/tables incl. sideways + subfloats) must be referenced from the text (\ref/\autoref/\cref-family); appendix exhibits marked (the A.13 rule proper). Runs on the MASTER-resolved document (auto-discovers the \documentclass master that inputs the checked file; resolves \input/\include recursively; comments stripped so a commented-out citation doesn't count). Registered as the exhibit-refs plan gate — deliberately NOT in the per-edit hook (exhibits legitimately exist before the prose that cites them; Kai's exhibits-first workflow would false-RED mid-draft). 7-scenario battery incl. cross-file orphan caught via the master; end-to-end RED→GREEN proven through spec_gate.
  • /work — the lead-orchestrator skill (new, skills/work/). The driver for the plan-file system, interview-designed with Kai (4 decisions): standalone skill with auto-trigger + explicit /work; micro-plan (auto-approved) for small tasks, full plan + condensed-chat sign-off for large (section-level / multi-artifact / multi-skill), trivia exempt; per unit: dispatch the EXISTING skill → deterministic gates (spec-gate registry) → three independent refute-by-default review lenses (conformance / faithfulness / argument — always all three, Kai's call) with recorded, auto-staling probe verdicts → bounded improvement (≤3 rounds, then escalate); plan_verify blocks "done" until every promised artifact exists + passed. Ships references/plan-template.md (smoke-tested end-to-end); kai-writing carries the routing pointer. Parser hardening en route: a YAML error in a plan now fails closed with the offending line instead of a raw traceback.

  • figure-review proof-of-sight gate. review-figure/scripts/figure_review_gate.py — manifest stamps a fresh render (per-image md5/mtime/dims); validate REJECTS (exit 3) a review report that lacks each page's md5 + name, killing the stale-crop / pattern-matched-pages failure KG caught by screenshot. Fail-closed; 8/8 able-to-fail battery (incl. stale-md5 rejection). Wired the A–E protocol into review-figure SKILL.md. The review-half of the research figure-gate (conformance half inbound from uam).

Spine drafted; being augmented by ai-org (agent-economy) + lp (slide-iteration) via coord. Foundation for the lead-orchestrator design of KG's workflow (problem 1 + 2).

New install/bootstrap-mac.sh + install/MAC-SETUP.md: Homebrew-driven install of R / Python (Miniconda) / Quarto / LaTeX / gh / pandoc, deploy to ~/.claude/, then the manual steps. Fresh-clone flow; a --check preflight (verifies every Homebrew name, installs nothing); non-fatal installs with an end-of-run summary; hardened after an adversarial review.

docs.title: 2026-07-09 — kai-theme: one colour+type spec, generated bindings, enforced by a gate
docs.text:
Kai's locked visual identity, designed via an interactive gallery and made a mechanism rather than a memo. New top-level theme/: - kai_theme.yaml — the single language-neutral source of truth. Two schemes: Kai-contrast (slate · crimson · pumpkin; lecture default) and Kai-elegant (wine · petrol · lavender; seminar default); old-gold fill-only; Beamer type 16/11/9/6 with a role-aware floor (6pt = sources only); coefficients and standard errors the same size. - gen_bindings.py generates theme_kai.R (ggplot), kai_theme.py (matplotlib), kai_theme.sty (Beamer) FROM the yaml — no hand-typed hexes; --check gates staleness in CI. - theme_conformance.py — the enforcement gate: flags any saturated hex not in the palette (catches stock ggplot/matplotlib blue). 8/8 able-to-fail battery, in CI. - Wired into install.sh/install.ps1 (ships theme/ to ~/.claude/) and the figure/writing skills (real-data-figure, map-figure, simulation-figure, tikz-figure, kai-writing) now point at the theme + the gate. Global ~/.claude/CLAUDE.md carries a canonical Visual-identity section. - talks 1.7.0 → 1.7.1: the old "20pt floor / 24pt target" font rule was PowerPoint-scale (renders ~2× too big in Beamer); replaced everywhere with the Beamer-pt scale + role-aware floor.

Lecture-pipeline figure migration (usg_theme.R → the theme) is coordinated separately with that session; the paper (muted / B&W-safe) register is still being designed.

docs.title: 2026-07-06 — install.sh --link: opt-in junction/symlink install mode
docs.text: Optimization #5 (the ARCHITECTURE "deferred" note, delivered as OPT-IN so default install behavior is untouched days before the Mac transition). bash install/install.sh --link installs ~/.claude items as Windows junctions / POSIX symlinks into the repo clone -- installed state and repo become the same files, eliminating the drift class permanently; re-run without the flag to revert to copies. The dangerous part -- removing a junction without recursing into the repo -- is handled by reparse-point-aware removal (cmd rmdir semantics, never rm -rf through a link) and PROVEN by a new 11-check battery (test_install_link.sh) whose load-bearing assertion is "repo file count unchanged after revert"; the battery also runs in CI (ubuntu = symlink branch; local = junction branch). Path conversion via cygpath (handles MSYS virtual paths like /tmp). PowerShell installer stays copy-only for now (noted; git-bash install.sh works on Windows for link mode).

docs.title: 2026-07-06 — Trigger-routing pass: descriptions verified by a blind 16-phrase router eval

docs.text: The last hardcoded-path class, gone before the Mac arrives: 26 files across academic-workflow (v1.24.1), project-workflow (v1.46.1), spec-gate (v0.2.1), stata-research-workflow (v1.6.1), kai-writing, templates, and the canonical structure doc. docs.title: 2026-07-06 — kai-writing: the structure -> leads -> paragraphs STAGE-GATE (Kai-flagged enforcement)
docs.text: Kai's drafting discipline was a prose rule and it decayed exactly as prose rules do: mid-session, id-mining free-drafted a section in the wrong voice, rationalizing a merge as "not writing" (manuscript-drafting-stage-gate thread; Kai flagged it himself). Now a mechanism in kai-writing: section-level work passes Stage A STRUCTURE (skeleton -> Kai signs off) -> Stage B LEAD SENTENCES (-> sign-off) -> Stage C PARAGRAPHS (the internal drafter/critic/rewriter pipeline runs within stages, never across gates). The "restructuring exemption" is closed BY NAME (new sentences = writing, however the task is framed), the gate ladder re-states itself at every transition (self-reground against long-session decay), and single-paragraph surgery correctly skips the gate. The skill description now hard-triggers on editing/appending/merging manuscript prose.

docs.title: 2026-07-05 — scientific-writing-analysis: the missing Lebrun codebook rebuilt from source
docs.text: The skill had ALWAYS shipped SKILL.md-only: it references references/diagnostic-codebook.md, references/book-examples.md, and scripts/lead_sentence_extractor.py, but those files never existed — not in the repo, not in git history, and not in the anthropic-skills bundle it was adapted from (which is itself SKILL.md-only). Every run silently fell back to Lebrun-from-memory (id-mining flagged the degradation). Now built faithfully from Kai's copy of Lebrun (2007), Scientific Writing: A Reader and Writer's Guide + Nikolov (2013): diagnostic-codebook.md (882 lines — every C/D/E ID the SKILL cites, grounded in the book with chapter/page pointers; the 4 E-entries honestly flagged as econ-augmentations, not Lebrun), book-examples.md (322 lines of the book's own worked before/after examples, page-cited), and a tested lead_sentence_extractor.py. SKILL.md gains a fail-LOUDLY guard so a missing reference file announces reduced-fidelity mode instead of silently degrading. Two build agents + faithfulness spot-checks against the extracted text (the "Tom Smith broken couple" p.14 and "happily wedded couples" verified verbatim).

docs.title: 2026-07-05 — irb-application skill ships: the pipeline is complete (experiment-methods v0.6.0)
docs.text: The final third of design -> pre-register -> ETHICS. Review-route triage as a decision node (European university committee — Kai's route, Bern then HSG — vs US IRB exempt/expedited/full incl. the 46.104(d)(3) benign-behavioral category; the Swiss HRA non-medical carve-out is presented as reasoning for THE COMMITTEE'S determination, never asserted). Drafts the committee-agnostic protocol substance — procedures, recruitment, actual consent TEXT for online studies, honest risks, the deception-vs-obfuscation line (econ no-deception norm; a real deception requires the menu + a debriefing plan), payments, a GDPR/FADP data-protection section (Prolific IDs are pseudonymous; anonymization before the replication deposit), vulnerable-population screen — plus the optional Asiedu et al. (2021) structured ethics appendix, and a CONSISTENCY GATE against design_spec.yaml + the pre-registration (mismatches flagged, never silently harmonized). Hard rules: never invent committee names, approval numbers, or legal determinations. References: irb_kai.md profile + ethics-guide.md. Blind planted-flaw smoke test at build.

docs.title: 2026-07-05 — pre-registration skill ships; preregister absorbed (experiment-methods v0.5.0, academic-workflow v1.23.0)

docs.title: 2026-07-05 — Toolpaths: sessions always know where the tools live (install/detect_toolpaths.sh)

docs.text: Found while integration-testing the resolver rewiring: the raw-data guard scanned only the content of a Write/Edit, never its file_path — so a Write aimed directly at data/raw/x.csv (the most blatant raw-data violation) sailed through silently. docs.title: 2026-07-05 — Hook portability: run_py.sh resolver (project-workflow v1.46.0, spec-gate v0.2.0)
docs.text: Mac-transition hardening. All 7 hook commands across the two hook-shipping plugins used to hardcode /c/ProgramData/anaconda3/python.exe — on macOS/Linux (or any Windows box without Anaconda) every guard silently no-oped. They now launch through hooks/run_py.sh, a POSIX-sh resolver: KTC_PYTHON override -> python3 -> python (Windows-Store stub rejected) -> known Anaconda/Homebrew/miniforge/system locations -> fail OPEN silently (a guard that cannot run must never block a session). One identical copy per plugin (self-contained installs); release_check.sh now mechanically enforces copy-identity and greps hooks.json for any reintroduced hardcoded python path (both proven able-to-fail). Verified: 7/7 resolver battery (test_run_py.sh: passthrough of args/stdin/exit-codes, override precedence, fail-open on stripped PATH, stub rejection), all 7 rewired commands integration-run rc=0, guards proven to STILL FIRE through the shim (clutter payload -> ask), existing batteries green (27 guard-smoke, 15 container-escape).

docs.title: 2026-07-05 — Cross-platform R environment installer (install/setup_r_environment.R)
docs.text: One canonical, idempotent R-package installer/verifier for everyone who uses the R analysis skills — and the smooth-start piece for new machines (Kai's MacBook next week included). Rscript install/setup_r_environment.R installs only what is missing from a grouped manifest (core / econ / tables / figures + optional maps / interactive / compiled), binary-first on Windows+macOS (no compiler needed), user-library only (no admin), ASCII output, exit 0 only when all required packages are present. --check reports without changing anything; --all adds the optional groups; fwildclusterboot is classified compiled-optional with a per-OS hint (Rtools / xcode-select) instead of a failure. Wired into both installers: install.sh and install.ps1 now run the --check report when R is found (the ps1 also probes C:\Program Files\R\R-* for off-PATH Windows installs) and print the one-line install command — never blocking the main install. Documented in install-toolkit.md Step 5 (incl. the new-Mac path). Verified on Windows R 4.4.3: check correctly flagged 2 missing required packages (exit 1), installed them, re-check exit 0; bash and PowerShell syntax checks pass.

docs.title: 2026-07-05 — 2026-07 audit Wave 1: mechanical fixes, trigger routing, docs freshness
