docs.text: The mechanical batch from the four-auditor toolkit audit (full report: working/toolkit-audit-2026-07.md; raw findings in working/audit-2026-07/): - No-stars is now the encoded default in /regression, /data-analysis, and the Stata conventions — implementing the existing fragment-table house style; stars are an explicit opt-in with a journal-requires-them note. Removed the false "stars match AER defaults" claim (the AER Style Guide bans asterisks). - Trigger routing: real-data-figure frontmatter no longer claims choropleths (routes to map-figure); personal-tier referee-report/coarse-review and the plugin's /review-paper now carry explicit yours-vs-someone-else's boundaries; kai-writing vs scientific-writing-analysis boundary sharpened (produce/revise vs diagnose). - Docs freshness: skill-reference regenerated (41/44 carded — spec-gate, meeting-notes, review-figure, kai-pedagogical-writing now present); skills-by-family gains the missing entries; notes-and-feedback contradiction fixed (meeting-notes shipped; notes are local-only); ARCHITECTURE counts corrected; docs/plans/ moved out of the published site to working/site-plans/; what-you-have-after-install added to the nav; marketplace description for experiment-methods updated to v0.4.x reality; CHANGELOG entry order fixed. - Hygiene: install.sh/.ps1 no longer ship *-workspace/ dev dirs to co-authors; acknowledgements now credit Lebrun, OWID/Gapminder, the talks canon, and point at the inline methods citations.

docs.title: 2026-07-05 -- 2026-07 audit Wave 2: econometrics currency as decision nodes (r-research-workflow v1.6.0, experiment-methods v0.4.1, academic-workflow v1.22.1)
docs.text:
Executes Wave 2 of the 2026-07 toolkit audit (working/toolkit-audit-2026-07.md section 3; findings in working/audit-2026-07/C-econ-standards.md). Framing rule (Kai, 2026-07-03): every method added here is DECISION-SUPPORT, never auto-applied -- the skill detects the situation, presents 2-4 options with pros AND cons AND citations, and ASKS; TWFE and CR1 clustered SEs remain what runs unless the researcher chooses otherwise.

  • (a) Staggered DiD: new r-research-workflow/rules/staggered-did.md -- estimator decision node (keep TWFE / fixest::sunab / Callaway-Sant'Anna did / BJS didimputation; dCDH named for non-absorbing treatment), Roth-Sant'Anna-Bilinski-Poe (2023) framing, HonestDiD (Rambachan-Roth 2023) offered as a pre-trends sensitivity option. Decision node wired into /regression Phase 3; estimator-labelled event-study variant in /coef-plot; r-reviewer flags staggered timing + plain TWFE with no documented choice.
  • (b) Weak IV: /regression retires the F<10 screen -- effective F (Montiel Olea-Pflueger 2013), Lee et al. (2022) tF benchmark, AR confidence sets; tested ivDiag recipe; options table when weak.
  • (c) Few clusters (R side): decision node (G < ~40-50 / few treated / unbalanced, per MacKinnon-Nielsen-Webb 2023) -- WCR bootstrap via fwildclusterboot (recipe marked UNTESTED: no R 4.4 Windows binary, no Rtools on the dev box) or CR2+Satterthwaite via clubSandwich (tested). Clustering rationale upgraded to the design-based rule (Abadie-Athey-Imbens-Wooldridge 2023; CGM 2008).
  • (d) MHT reachability: /regression bullet (Romano-Wolf / Anderson 2008 index / justified none, offered not defaulted) + experiment-design D7 completeness-gate checkbox for secondary/mechanism outcome families.
  • (e) RDD: r-code-conventions package table gains rdrobust + rddensity with the manipulation-test one-liner (Cattaneo-Idrobo-Titiunik).
  • (f) Environment capture: templates/00_setup.R (kt-template-version 2026-07-05) writes sessionInfo() to output/session_info.txt on every run (AEA environment-documentation floor); /init-replication offers renv as an explicit option (never initialized unasked).
  • (g) docs/submissions.md: new "Disclosure statements the journal will require" section -- Elsevier generative-AI declaration, AEA COI disclosure policy (AEA has no generative-AI policy as of 2026-07).

Gates run: all shipped R recipes executed on synthetic fixtures via Rscript 4.4.3 (sunab, did/att_gt+aggte, didimputation, HonestDiD, fitstat ivf1/ivwald1, ivDiag, clubSandwich, rdrobust, rddensity, plus the coef-plot CS plotting recipe) -- 2 recipes marked UNTESTED in code comments (fwildclusterboot, DIDmultiplegtDYN: not installable on R 4.4.3 Windows without Rtools); templates test harness 15 PASS / 0 FAIL (Stata cases skipped, unrelated); test_theme.R 9/9; mkdocs build --strict clean.

docs.title: 2026-07-03 — experiment-design: type-branched structure + design graphs + background bundle (experiment-methods v0.4.0)
docs.text: Kai chose option A: one /experiment-design skill with a shared interview spine, branched depth by experiment TYPE. - Deep, validated track = online survey / information experiments (Kai's domain). Field-RCT and lab are branched roadmap stubs — references/design-methods-field-rct.md and design-methods-lab.md — held per Kai (lab + RCT on hold, to-do). D1 classifies the type; for field/lab the skill tells the user the track is roadmap-only and offers the shared spine with a caveat rather than faking survey depth. - Bundled the deep background — the 393-line pre-registration/IRB/design synthesis (with all sources) is now references/background-and-sources.md. - Design/process graphs now offered at D7 — a CONSORT participant-flow diagram + a design-timeline schematic, routed to tikz-figure (results figures still go to /descriptives + /coef-plot).

docs.title: 2026-07-03 — experiment-design deepened + validated 7/7 (experiment-methods v0.3.0)
docs.text: Second Kai-personalization round (Virality exemplar + his stated rules), plus a blind validation test: - Never assume — options with pros AND cons AND a citation; the human decides (hard constraint; fishing "what's your default?" questions are out). - Randomization is a CONTINGENT decision — diagnosed per experiment, no fixed default; Lin (2013) covariate adjustment as the analysis invariant. - Always pilot & pre-test before fielding; incentive size calibrated from the pilot; HALT if a changed design reaches hand-off without one. - Platform QC (Prolific): fair/high pay, no bot screen (Peer et al. 2022), representativeness quotas per case; strong comprehension checks but NEVER post-treatment exclusion — primary = ITT, comprehension → pre-registered subsample/LATE (Montgomery-Nyhan-Torres 2018); light pre-randomization attention checks. - Completeness gate at D7 — a mandatory 16-point checklist flags any MISSING element before emitting (the "remind me if I forgot something" mechanism). Validated: a blind planted-flaw review test caught 7/7 seeded flaws (3 HALT, 4 HIGH) with correct grades + citations, plus 4 unplanted real issues. Still local; pre-registration + irb-application follow.

docs.title: 2026-07-03 — experiment-design deepened + citation-verified (experiment-methods v0.2.0)
docs.text: A Kai-personalization interview turned the v0.1.0 flagship from a best-practice summary into Kai's skill, and an adversarial claim-verifier pass hardened its citations: - Prior elicitation OFF by default — eliciting the outcome's prior primes/anchors/biases outcome choice; the randomized control group is the counterfactual. HRW's "elicit priors" advice is re-scoped to belief-updating (information-provision) estimands only, with its mitigations. (Kai's correction.) - Randomization is a contingent decision, not a default — simple / stratified / rerandomize chosen from the experiment's characteristics; Lin (2013) covariate adjustment is the invariant analysis. - Hard interaction rule — never assume; every choice is options with pros AND cons AND a citation, and the researcher decides (no fishing questions). - Pilot + pre-test mandatory — incentive size calibrated from the pilot; HALT if a changed design reaches hand-off without one. Noisy-outcome power = pool several studies with a pre-specified pooled MDE; no naive optional stopping (inflates FPR ~0.05→~0.15; valid only via pre-specified group-sequential/alpha-spending). - Citation verification: a claim-verifier checked every reference for existence AND claim-match — 17 VERIFIED, 0 detail errors, and 1 corrected overstatement (Lin now reads "cannot hurt asymptotic precision," not "guarantees a gain" — the theorem is no-harm, not must-gain). The quantitative claims (700/arm, 0.13 SD, 0.05→0.15) were verified against the source PDFs.

docs.title: 2026-07-02 — New plugin: experiment-methods (v0.1.0) — /experiment-design flagship
docs.text: First skill of a 3-skill family (design → pre-registration → irb-application) for economists running primary-data experiments — from pp's handoff, expanded by Kai. /experiment-design designs a survey or field experiment end-to-end through conversation, in two modes: design-from-scratch (interview, one question at a time, propose-and-react) or review (critique an existing design against the checklist). Grounded in the economics design canon (Haaland-Roth-Wohlfart 2023, Stantcheva 2023, Harrison-List 2004, Duflo-Glennerster-Kremer, List-Sadoff-Wagner 2011, de Quidt et al. 2018, Bruhn-McKenzie 2009, McKenzie 2012) with a real worked exemplar (Gehring & Grigoletto, "Virality"). Enforces the load-bearing rules first-draft designs most often miss: an incentivized primary outcome and a matched/active control. Emits a structured design_spec.yaml + design_spec.md that hands off to the (forthcoming) pre-registration and irb-application skills. Built via skill-creator; landscape research in working/experiment-methods-research.md. Manifests green (8 plugins registered). pre-registration + irb-application follow.

docs.title: 2026-07-02 — Session scratch relocated: temp_claude/ → .claude/tmp/ (project-workflow v1.45.0)
docs.text:
From pp's handoff (Podcast Persuasion): stop scaffolding a top-level temp_claude/. Canonical Claude session scratch is now .claude/tmp/ (gitignored) — at the project root for a single-root project, inside each clone (clone_XX/.claude/tmp/) for a multi-clone container, never a top-level folder. The rule is clone-agnostic (it holds with or without clones), per Kai: "scratch belongs inside .claude/, not as another top-level folder."

Updated: both canonical specs (principles/ master + plugins/ mirror), refactor_structure.py (forensic log + STANDARD_LAYOUT), the bootstrap-project scaffold + .gitignore, guard_clutter's exempt-list (adds .claude/tmp; temp_claude kept tolerated for legacy so existing projects are not newly flagged), the guard smoke test, build-exhibits-preview, the housekeeping SKILL, the r/stata code-conventions, and docs/templates. The container/clone/audit detection logic is intentionally untouched — a top-level scratch dir is still correctly flagged. Verified: 126 checks green (27 guard-smoke + 24 verify_container + 51 check_clone_discipline + 6 refactor_latex + 18 gen_handoff).

docs.title: 2026-07-02 — Coefficient-plot house style + output-type title branch (r-research-workflow v1.5.5)
docs.text: From id-mining's figure/exhibit notes (relaying Kai's stated conventions): - Coefficient plots carry significance geometrically — the CI vs the zero reference line IS the test. So: no significance stars, no colour-coding by significance, no "significant / not significant" legend. One uniform colour per single series; colour only for a real grouping (arms/specs/outcomes); a pooled/summary marker by shape. Stars stay in tables. New figure-design-rules §9.6 + the §3 line; coef-plot SKILL "Important" section; and r-reviewer gains a mechanical coefplot-significance check so it is enforced, not just documented. - Figure titles branch on output type (§9.1): a paper figure carries no in-graph headline (the descriptive title lives in the LaTeX \caption); a presentation figure states the finding on the slide. Same figure, different title placement. Fixed the coef-plot example titles from narrative to descriptive to match the paper default.

docs.title: 2026-07-02 — spec-gate: reusable anti-drift primitive (spec-gate v0.1.0, NEW plugin)
docs.text:
New plugin spec-gate — the fail-closed spec-gate + reground-on-cadence mechanism that every long build (lecture pipeline, ai-org research code, the writing routine, this marketplace) kept re-inventing, extracted once and generalized. A spec-gate/conditions.yaml turns the spec into a checkable list; spec_gate.py check runs it fail-closed; reground.py + cadence.py re-inject the load-bearing conditions on a cadence (SessionStart hook nudges when overdue, silent unless the project is governed).

  • Four check kinds: deterministic (shell exit code — the cheap default), probe (a judgement the runner can't make — an agent records a verdict keyed to a content-hash of the artefact, so an edit auto-stales it; the runner never spends tokens), material_read (every agent-visible text carries a current read-receipt), lock (check_locks.py — a credible-commitment ledger against OSCILLATION: a settled decision's file can't change without a logged entry citing the lock + new evidence).
  • Every kind proven able-to-fail — test_spec_gate.py shows each goes RED on a known-bad input (24/24); a check that can't fail is a tautology stub.
  • /spec-gate init scaffolds it into any pipeline.
  • Proven on a self-testable adopter (Option B): the marketplace's OWN build now has spec-gate/conditions.yaml (manifest validity + registration parity + the primitive's self-test + docs read-receipts + an independent probe of the SKILL) — all GREEN. No lock check: the marketplace has no oscillating decision to lock, so the lock kind is proven able-to-fail by the battery's git-forgery test rather than by locking a growing plugin set. The probe loop converged honestly 0.68 → 0.85, each round fixing a real doc gap an independent reviewer found, never lowering the bar to pass.
  • Hardened by a 3-lens adversarial review (false-GREEN hunt, design-fidelity/anti-theatre, security/robustness) before first commit. Two false-GREEN blockers found + fixed: material_read keyed on bare content hash (a never-read file passed if its bytes matched a signed-off one) → now keyed per (check_id, path, hash); the lock ledger was self-certifying (editing locks.yaml re-hid a reversal) → baseline now anchored in the git-HEAD-committed ledger, so re-hiding requires committing a forged ledger (a logged act). Plus: the SessionStart hook now fails OPEN on any exception (was crashing on missing pyyaml / malformed conditions.yaml); relock rejects empty evidence + stamps a real date; probe records require a --by judge (provenance); an optional selftest: per check enforces able-to-fail for adopter checks; streaming/​size-capped hashing; _state/ excluded from globs; atomic state writes. Every fix ships with a regression test (battery 35/35, hook 6/6) proving the attack is now RED.
  • Implements ~/.claude/principles/agentic-build-discipline.md U1–U7 as an installable mechanism (the anti-drift principle is now enforced by a mechanism, not decaying prose); that file now points at the plugin.

docs.title: 2026-06-26 — Glossary seeder for existing papers (academic-workflow v1.21.0)
docs.text:
Adds /bootstrap-paper --seed-glossary <paper.tex|dir> — bootstraps a paper's CONCEPTS.md from prose that already exists (the common case: the glossary feature postdates the paper). Interactive by design (Kai's pick over batch extraction), and strictly inside the naming-authority gate:

  • scripts/seed_glossary_candidates.py (new, +smoke test 7/7) does the deterministic half — strips LaTeX, counts recurring multi-word phrases + capitalized terms with counts and example lines. It writes nothing and makes no synonym call (that "documentary = narrative = the arm" judgment is semantic, left to the agent reading the prose + the author).
  • The skill then consults the author ONE concept at a time, leading with a proposed canonical term. An enforced (approved) row + its §7 Approval-log line are written ONLY on the author's same-turn confirmation; unsure → a proposed row; rejected → nothing. The seeder can count and propose; it can never canonize on its own.
  • Closes with check_glossary.py --audit to confirm every approved row is logged.

Completes the glossary feature set (lint gate + naming-authority rework + seeder). Sits on the v1.20.0 rework.

docs.title: 2026-06-26 — Glossary: naming-authority gate + auto-create/consult (academic-workflow v1.20.0)
docs.text:
Reworks the per-paper glossary after a 3-agent adversarial review found the naming authority structurally unmitigated: the canonical column was LLM-writable mid-turn, the "needs Kai's approval" rule was the only un-gated approval rule in the kit, and check_glossary.py trusted whatever was in the column — so a deterministic gate could launder and enforce an LLM's term choice, silently outranking the soft-enforced style guide. Plus: a missing or empty glossary passed "green" with zero consultation, and generic figure-style rules had leaked into the per-paper template. Kai's directive: the LLM must never adopt or propose a naming without checking with him, and the glossary must never override the writing guide.

The fix (audit-ledger mechanism, Kai's pick):

  • Status column on §1. Rows are proposed until Kai approves them (approved / KG YYYY-MM-DD). check_glossary.py enforces ONLY approved rows — a term an agent invents has no power over a draft until Kai signs it. Legacy glossaries with no Status column stay fully enforced (back-compat).
  • §7 Approval log + --audit. Approving a term means a dated, human-written ledger line; check_glossary.py --audit flags any approved row missing one, so a silently flipped Status is detectable.
  • Inactive gate is non-zero. No glossary / no approved terms now exits 2 (was 0) — a missing glossary can no longer pass as "clean."
  • kai-writing Stage 0. Loads-or-creates the glossary and consults Kai (one term at a time) BEFORE drafting; §1 is fed to drafters + critic; a new critic dimension raises concept-inconsistency to Kai instead of the rewriter silently canonicalizing.
  • Precedence clause in CONCEPTS.md, academic-writing.md (B8/A1/D3), and kai-writing: the glossary governs term choice only — never voice, the AI-tell lexicon, or dashes, which win on conflict. A canonical term that trips B8 is a defect to re-approve, not a term to enforce.
  • De-leak. §5 generic figure rules demoted to pointers (figure-design-rules / review-figure own them); bootstrap-paper scaffolds the guard + a populate step. check_glossary.py smoke test: 9/9 (propose-not-enforced, exit-2 inactive, legacy, audit both ways).

Ships the script with the version bump (the prior cache predated it). Seeder for existing papers (writes proposed rows only) is the next step.

docs.title: 2026-06-26 — Glossary: collapse to ONE file CONCEPTS.md (academic-workflow v1.19.0, project-workflow v1.41.0)
docs.text:
Reverses the earlier two-file glossary (terms.md + CONCEPTS.md) to a SINGLE CONCEPTS.md, on the strength of UAM's worked example — a week of real use, which made the case that one human-editable file is what actually gets maintained mid-session, and demonstrated the killer feature live (Kai's "drop 'marble', call it the utility function" → one edit to the canonical entry, then 17 exhibit/prose edits in one pass, zero drift). Kai's call after the worked example landed.

CONCEPTS.md now carries everything in a load-bearing order: §1 the canonical vocabulary table (the LINT TARGET), §2 the conceptual ordering / layers, §3 definitions, §4 relationships, §5 exhibit-label conventions (the operational heart — where "labels draw from the glossary" becomes a contract, and the home of the compute-don't-assert rule), §6 under-revision / open questions. The template + every reference were retargeted; templates/terms.md is deleted.

  • templates/CONCEPTS.md rewritten to the seven-section UAM shape with the §1 table + §5 banned-list (the lint reads both).
  • check_glossary.py now searches CONCEPTS.md first (then terms.md / KEY_TERMS.md for back-compat); parsing is unchanged (table banned-column + banned-list block). Smoke test retargeted, 5/5.
  • kai-writing, /bootstrap-paper, the CLAUDE-template "Paper glossary" block, /bootstrap-project, adversarial-review, review-figure, and /review-paper all updated from two-file to one-file and from "grep" to the check_glossary.py gate. No dangling terms.md references (only the intentional back-compat fallbacks remain).

Net: the glossary feature shipped earlier today is now the one-file shape its real-world worked example proved out, before the template hardened.

Still queued: the glossary SEEDER (Gap 1) — now unblocked by both the one-file decision and UAM's reference shape; drafts CONCEPTS.md from an existing paper's prose.

docs.title: 2026-06-26 — check_glossary.py deterministic banned-term gate (academic-workflow v1.18.0)
docs.text:
Hardens the glossary feature's enforcement (Gap 2 of the glossary follow-up): turns kai-writing's prose "grep the draft against the banned list" into a runnable lint with an exit code, because a soft "please grep" gets skipped — the exact failure id-mining reported (an abstract shipped "documentary"/"film" off-glossary).

plugins/academic-workflow/scripts/check_glossary.py: reads the banned terms from a paper's terms.md (both the fenced banned-list block AND the "Banned alternatives" column of the canonical-terms table, with the row's canonical term as the suggested replacement), scans a draft (.tex/.md/ .txt), and reports every banned term with its line number and the approved replacement. Exit 1 on any hit (so it gates a pre-output / pre-submission step), 0 when clean. Finds terms.md by walking up from the draft; skips LaTeX comment lines; word-boundary matching (so "filmography" doesn't trip "film"). When no glossary exists or no terms are pinned yet it warns (exit 0) that the gate is INACTIVE — not that the draft is clean. --json for programmatic use.

kai-writing's hard pre-output step now calls the script (with a manual-grep fallback if the plugin isn't installed). Regression-guarded by a 5-case smoke test (check_glossary_smoke_test.sh, 5/5: hits, word boundary, comment-skip, no-glossary, empty-glossary).

Next (Gap 1, designed but not built): a glossary SEEDER that drafts terms.md + CONCEPTS.md from an existing paper's prose, so papers that predate the glossary feature get one without hand-writing it from scratch.

docs.title: 2026-06-26 — Adversarial-reviewer-loop lessons (adversarial-review + academic-workflow v1.17.0)
docs.text:
Folds id-mining's writing-review-process-lessons Part B into the review skills — five failure modes from a real abstract-drafting session where the review loop produced staccato, voice-violating drafts and let accepted fixes regress.

adversarial-review gains a "Reviewing prose (papers, abstracts, proposals)" section + a sharpened persona in the prompt template:

  1. Real-reviewer persona — brief reviewers as the overloaded referee who skims ~20s and defaults to reject, not a friendly colleague. A soft "is this interesting and fair?" brief breeds cheerleaders.
  2. Agents CHECK; the author DECIDES voice + structure — pass the author's fixed constraints (voice, "the null is one sentence") as do-not-violate; agents flag against them, never restructure. Letting reviewer feedback drive the prose is how a draft ends up in the reviewers' voice.
  3. Don't-regress ledger across rounds — carry a CHANGES_LEDGER (the kai-writing pattern) and re-verify prior fixes each round; without it round 3 silently undoes round 1.
  4. Require ground truth + source access — hand the reviewer the tables / regression output / terms.md / CONCEPTS.md so it catches overclaims and terminology drift, not just taste.
  5. Style-auditor output is heuristic, not command — "split every compound into one idea" is advice applied with judgment, not a literal rule; applied mechanically it breaks a flowing voice.

Plus an optional "hostile editor + 3 referees + glossary check" panel preset carrying all five. /review-paper (academic-workflow v1.17.0) gains a pointer that applies the same five rules to its 6-agent panel — most importantly, handing every agent the ground-truth tables + the glossary (it already had a terminology-drift and an unsupported-claims agent; this makes the data available to all of them).

This completes the two cross-session reliability threads (UAM research-pipeline-reliability 3/3 + id-mining writing-review-process-lessons A + B).

docs.title: 2026-06-26 — Task-list nudge hook (project-workflow v1.40.0)
docs.text:
Addresses UAM's research-pipeline-reliability ask #1 — the model reliably forgets to maintain a running task list and ignores the periodic background reminder. Kai's call after I flagged that the harness hook model can't hard-block on conversation state (hooks see tool input, not the message, and can't call TaskList): ship it as a louder, better-targeted nudge rather than a hard stop.

New UserPromptSubmit hook nudge_task_list.py: when a submitted prompt looks clearly MULTI-PART, it injects a forceful reminder to make a TaskCreate/TaskUpdate pass before substantive work (capture each ask, mark one in_progress, append rather than overwrite on new mid-task feedback). It fires at exactly the moment a multi-part request arrives — not on a timer.

Calibrated to avoid nagging (a hook that cries wolf gets ignored, which is the very failure it targets): two-tier detection — explicit STRUCTURE (>= 2 numbered items, >= 2 bullets, or a "do X then Y then Z" sequence) fires at any length; softer signals (one list marker, sequencer words like "also", a "first ... then", two or more distinct questions) fire only above ~120 chars and only when >= 2 are present. Silent on short asks, single requests, long single questions, and version/decimal noise (v1.40.0, 3.14). Best-effort: any parse trouble allows silently. Wired into project-workflow/hooks/hooks.json as the first UserPromptSubmit hook. Regression-guarded by an 8-case smoke test (nudge_task_list_smoke_test.sh, 8/8) — which caught three real calibration gaps during the build (inline numbered lists, sub-length-gate bullet lists, single-signal multi-step sequences).

This is a nudge, not a hard block — the hook model can't enforce a TaskCreate pass deterministically. If the harness later exposes conversation state to hooks, this can be upgraded to a real gate.

docs.title: 2026-06-26 — New skill review-figure + no-hard-coded-labels rule (r-research-workflow v1.5.0)
docs.text:
Addresses UAM's research-pipeline-reliability ask #2 — the dominant failure of a long figure session: figures shown with labels that did not match the data (a facet titled "rises with upgrading-readiness" that was actually a V-shape; a category in the wrong group; "HC1 SE" jargon on an axis; a whole pairwise comparison missing). Root cause is structural: the author cannot proofread their own figure (curse of knowledge — the maker sees intent, not the page).

Two enforcement points, as UAM framed them:

  • The rule (compute, don't assert). figure-design-rules §4 gains a hard gate: no hard-coded semantic/directional label. A label that asserts a property of the data ("rises", "significant", a group name, a treatment assignment, an axis abbreviation for a concept) must be COMPUTED from the data and printed, then written from the printout — never typed from intent. §5 gains the compute-then-label R pattern (group-wise slope/shape printout before titling a facet). real-data-figure step 6 carries the same rule.
  • The cold-eyes critic. New top-level skill review-figure: a FRESH sub-agent (context=fork, so it never sees the maker's intent) receives the RENDERED figure AND the underlying numbers and is told to FIND errors — label-vs-data mismatch (recomputed from the data), jargon, wrong encodings, overlaps/cut-offs, unsupported claims, missing comparisons, and terminology that deviates from the paper glossary (terms.md / CONCEPTS.md). It grades BLOCK/HIGH/MED/LOW and BLOCKS the figure until clean. It is the figure analogue of the prose editor-agent, but data-grounded: it requires the numbers, not just the image (image-only reviews are downgraded — they can't verify a label against the data). real-data-figure now dispatches it as the final gate before declaring a figure done — the figure-side equivalent of the CoVe post-flight check.

Boundaries written to avoid collision: review-figure reviews (not produces — that's real-data-figure/coef-plot), is data-grounded (unlike the general adversarial-review), and is correctness+clarity (not palette/house-style, which figure-design-rules + the r-reviewer cover). docs/INDEX.md regenerated (42 skills).

Still queued from the two threads: the task-list-discipline hook (UAM #1) and the adversarial-reviewer-loop lessons (id-mining B).

docs.title: 2026-06-26 — Per-paper glossary feature (academic-workflow v1.16.0, project-workflow v1.39.0)
docs.text:
Builds the per-paper glossary both UAM (research-pipeline-reliability) and id-mining (writing-review-process-lessons) asked for — the item Kai flagged as central. Closes a silent-gate bug: kai-writing globbed KEY_TERMS.md while the house-style glossary is terms.md, so the terminology check never fired and prose drifted off-vocabulary undetected (a real abstract shipped "documentary"/"film" off-glossary).

Two files (Kai's design call): paper/terms.md is the controlled vocabulary and the LINT TARGET (canonical term, banned alternatives, dash / italics conventions); paper/CONCEPTS.md is the concept model (each concept defined + the relationships between them), from which figure/table labels and recurring prose terms draw their meaning. terms.md fixes the wording; CONCEPTS.md fixes the meaning.

Changes:

  • kai-writing — globs {terms,CONCEPTS,KEY_TERMS}.md (back-compat for existing KEY_TERMS projects; new projects use terms.md). Documents the two-file model. Adds a HARD pre-output step: load terms.md, conform the draft, then GREP the draft against the banned list (don't trust memory) and report the hit count (0 to ship). Completeness rule: pin every recurring term incl. object nouns + units; keep the file a clean glossary, not a sweep log. Pipeline checklist updated to the grep gate.
  • New templates templates/terms.md + templates/CONCEPTS.md — seeded scaffolds with <PAPER> placeholders, a banned-list block for the grep, and a relationships section that figures must stay consistent with.
  • /bootstrap-paper (academic-workflow v1.16.0) — scaffolds both glossary files alongside paper_structure.md; explains the lint-target vs concept- model split and why the filename makes the gate fire.
  • CLAUDE template + /bootstrap-project (project-workflow v1.39.0) — a new paper-conditional "## Paper glossary" block makes terms.md + CONCEPTS.md a mandatory read in the project's CLAUDE.md (id-mining's "a session never loads it" fix), so the rule travels to co-authors independent of any skill. Included only for projects that produce a paper. Also fixed a stale "five hard rules" → "seven" drift in bootstrap-project's core-conventions description.
  • adversarial-review — Paper-draft attack surface gains "terminology drift off terms.md"; Figure surface gains "label-vs-data mismatch" + "jargon on axes"; a new note instructs feeding terms.md + CONCEPTS.md into every reviewer's context (id-mining A4: reviewers had the numbers but not the glossary, so they never caught the drift).

Still queued from the same two threads: the review-figure cold-eyes critic + no-hardcoded-semantic-labels rule (UAM #2), the task-list-discipline hook (UAM #1), and the adversarial-reviewer-loop lessons (id-mining B).

docs.title: 2026-06-26 — Referee-skill family: cross-document consistency pass (academic-workflow v1.15.0)
docs.text:
Ran the pedagogical/consistency critic over the four-document referee family (referee-reply-style.md + /format-referee-reports + /respond-to-referees + /reply-to-editor). The boundary tables, numbering scheme, firewall rule, load-profile-first instruction, and CoVe were all already aligned; the critic caught real divergences worth fixing:

  • /respond-to-referees Step 4 (the HIGH one). The operative drafting instruction described a flatter 4-step structure that DROPPED the reply arc's defining beat — "establish common understanding / restate the concern charitably" — and even said "no paraphrasing flattery," contradicting the same skill's own load-first paragraph and the canonical arc in referee-reply-style.md §6. (Cause: this skill predates the style profile; Step 4 was never reconciled when the profile was wired in.) Rewrote Step 4 to the full 5-beat arc and replaced "no paraphrasing flattery" with the charitable-restatement-is-not-flattery distinction.
  • /respond-to-referees output target. Step 5 produced a standalone working/response-to-referees-*.md while the skill's intro said it writes INTO the \emph{Reply: [TO BE DRAFTED]} TeX slots that /format-referee-reports creates. Reconciled: fill the TeX slots in the chain case (when paper/revisions/<JOURNAL>/ exists), produce the standalone markdown only when invoked without the scaffold.
  • /format-referee-reports Step 1 forward-referenced /respond-to-referees's conversion table — but it runs FIRST in the chain. Inlined its own 4-row table so it stands alone.
  • Person rule ("I" solo / "we" co-authored, per the style profile) was missing from /respond-to-referees and /reply-to-editor; added to both.
  • Cosmetic: the "Three vs Four referee-shaped skills" count disagreed across the trio (all three boundary tables list four rows); standardized on "Four (one pre-submission, three for the R&R)".

Also bumped academic-workflow to v1.15.0 (the v1.14.0 /format-referee-reports ship missed its bump) and regenerated docs/INDEX.md so the new referee skills appear in the public command/skill list (both honestly marked HALTED until their real-R&R smoke test).

docs.title: 2026-06-25 — New skill /format-referee-reports + wire style profile
docs.text:
New skill for R&R workspace setup: takes the journal's as-received referee reports + editor decision letter and produces three artefacts in one pass.

  1. TeX-ified referee reports under paper/revisions/<JOURNAL>/ (the Overleaf-synced revision workspace from the submissions convention), with referee comments in upright text and \emph{Reply: [TO BE DRAFTED]} slots in italic for co-authors to fill. Numbering streamlined to the canonical R<n>.<m>.<letter> (R1.5.a, R2.7.c) regardless of how the referee numbered, with the original numbering kept as a parenthetical for traceability.
  2. Internal clustering doc at working/referee_clusters_<JOURNAL>_R<round>.md (gitignored) — groups similar comments across reviewers under shared themes (identification, external validity, etc.), names conflicts where two referees ask for incompatible things, proposes resolutions for the co-author discussion.
  3. Internal per-comment tasks table at working/referee_tasks_<JOURNAL>_R<round>.md (gitignored) — one row per comment with five columns: By / Referee comment / Comments / space to discuss / Steps we undertake / Taken or Done. The discuss column is the firewall: internal co-author critique that never reaches the journal. The skill draft-populates Steps but leaves discuss blank by default (the LLM doesn't auto-fill that column — it's meant for human discussion).

Bookends the existing referee toolchain so the four skills cover the full R&R lifecycle with clear boundaries:

Stage Skill Pre-submission review of your own draft /review-paper Just received decision; set up the R&R workspace /format-referee-reports (NEW) Drafting per-referee replies /respond-to-referees Drafting the editor cover letter /reply-to-editor

All three R&R skills now explicitly load plugins/academic-workflow/rules/referee-reply-style.md (shipped 2026-06-24) for uniform typography, numbering, tone, and the firewall rule. Each carries a "boundary triple" table in its SKILL.md routing the user to the right neighbour for the wrong stage.

HALTED on ship (disable-model-invocation: true) — pairs with /respond-to-referees and /reply-to-editor, which are already HALTED for the same reason. All three should un-halt together once a real R&R round provides smoke-test material (the CoVe verification path for the drafting skills + the TeX-ification + clustering pipeline for this one). Explicit invocation via /format-referee-reports still works.

Trigger-collision audit verified: all three referee skills carry the HALT - DO NOT AUTO-FIRE prefix in their descriptions, so auto-fire is structurally disabled until smoke-tested. /review-paper is clearly distinguished by "pre-submission" and "before I submit" cues; the boundary triple table in each SKILL.md surfaces the timing distinction explicitly.

docs.title: 2026-06-24 — Bug fixes from end-to-end testing of two shipped skills
docs.text:
End-to-end runtime tests on /lit-corpus (marker engine) and /meeting-notes (two-pass extraction with adversarial transcript) caught real defects in code that was already pushed. Fixed forward; no version bumps because the public API is unchanged.

/lit-corpus — flipped the default engine from marker back to fast (pymupdf4llm). Marker was set as the default in v1.37.0 based on benchmark research but had never been run on Kai's CPU-only Windows/Anaconda box. The end-to-end test produced Failed: 1, New/updated: 0 — zero output. Direct invocation surfaced the cause: a MemoryError during marker's import chain (marker pulls torch + transformers + surya + google-genai, OOMing before a single page is converted). The shipped default cannot fail on the maintainer's own machine; fast is reliable, zero-install, and works. Marker is now opt-in with an explicit caveat: try it locally, confirm a populated .md, and only then rely on it. The first-use download estimate is also corrected (the shipped CHANGELOG said "~1 GB"; actual is several GB across layout + recognition + table + detection + ocr-error + inline-math models).

/meeting-notes — four script-level fixes from the e2e tester's report:

  1. Confidentiality blocklist redesigned (HIGH). The shipped blocklist fired on the bare word referee (and the pattern referee\s+\d) in transcript content, so a routine R&R-planning call saying "if Referee 2 pushes again on external validity" tripped a triple confidentiality match and HALTed — exactly the call the skill exists to handle. Now there are two asymmetric channels: a PATH channel uses the bare keywords (a filename you chose containing "reviewer"/"panel"/"grades"/"medical"/"hiring" is a real signal), and a CONTENT channel uses only high-precision regexes — explicit confidentiality declarations (\bconfidential\b, "do not distribute/circulate/forward/share", "in strict confidence", "embargoed"), a line-start referee/reviewer REPORT header ((?m)^\s*\**\s*(?:referee| reviewer)\s*#?\s*\d — catches a pasted report, not mid-sentence mention), and precise multi-word phrases that don't collide with econ vocabulary (hiring committee, funding panel, student grade, medical record). Verified: R&R-planning call CLEAN, pasted referee report FIRES, reviewer_2_report.vtt FIRES on path, "CONFIDENTIAL — do not distribute" FIRES on content.
  2. write accepts --metadata-file / --action-items-file. The shipped --metadata / --action-items accept raw JSON via argv, but on Windows the transcript_path field carries backslashes (C:\Users\…) and gets mangled passing through the shell, producing JSONDecodeError: Invalid \escape. File-based input sidesteps shell quoting entirely. The clean realistic pattern (verified end-to-end) is to redirect parse stdout straight to a file and pass that file to write --metadata-file — no re-serialization, no escaping. The inline forms still work for non-Windows paths; the SKILL spec is updated to recommend the file-based forms.
  3. write enforces metadata presence. Previously both --metadata and --metadata-file were optional with no guard, so an invocation that forgot both crashed inside json.loads(None). Now refuses cleanly with a pointer to the file-based form.
  4. TODO line word-order + dead counter. Conditional action items rendered as "...by [DATE NOT NAMED] [Condition: ...]" which reads oddly; reshuffled to "... [Condition: ...] by [DATE NOT NAMED]". The dead tentative_decisions counter (counted tentative over action_items, but tentative is a decision property; decisions never reach write) was renamed to tentative_action_items so the JSON name matches the field it actually counts. The note rendering already handles the [DECISION TENTATIVE] tag through the LLM-built note body, not through this counter.

Referee-reply style profile shipped (plugins/academic-workflow/rules/ referee-reply-style.md) — load-bearing reference encoding Kai's conventions from published reply letters (APSR, AEJ Applied, AEJ Policy, World Development): typography (referee normal, reply italic, Reply: prefix), streamlined 5.a/7.c numbering regardless of the referee's scheme, the internal clustering doc that groups similar comments across reviewers, the per-comment tasks table with its "Comments / space to discuss" firewall column (internal co-author critique that never reaches the journal), the hyperfriendly reply arc (warm thanks → common understanding → what we do + what it shows → exact location → optional flexibility), CoVe on every location claim, and confidentiality rules. The next-step referee skills (/respond-to-referees, /reply-to-editor, the queued R&R formatter) will all load this; not wired yet, just shipped.

docs.title: 2026-06-23 — New skill /reply-to-editor (academic-workflow v1.14.0)
docs.text:
Standalone editor cover-letter generator for R&R submissions. Distinct from /respond-to-referees (which produces the per-referee response document); the editor letter is shorter, addresses the editor's specific decision-letter points rather than forwarded referee comments, and lives separately at the journal portal.

Inputs: editor decision letter (PDF/docx/txt) + revised manuscript (for CoVe verification) + optional response-to-referees document (used to ground the "summary of main changes" bullets in real revisions already drafted).

Workflow: - Step 1 tags decision-letter content as editor-specific concerns vs forwarded referee comments vs procedural requests; only the first class drives substantive responses. - Step 2 composes a 3-5 bullet summary of main changes (the cover letter's most-read paragraph). Draws from the response-to-referees Concern Matrix if available; otherwise from a manuscript diff or scan. - Step 3 drafts 3-5 sentence responses to each editor-specific concern, addressed in second person, courteous + brief. - Step 4 renders to working/cover_letter_<journal>_R<round>.{md,tex} using the new templates/editor-cover-letter.md template. - Step 5 runs MANDATORY CoVe post-flight verification on every "we added X on page Y" claim via the existing claim-verifier agent + post-flight-verification rule (shared with /respond-to-referees). - Step 6 surfaces unresolved concerns in the final chat message (NOT in the cover letter).

Tone conventions baked in: editor letter is the cover-letter first impression, so courteous + confident + brief; no scope-expansion promises the manuscript doesn't deliver; no lengthy quoting of referees; Kai's external-communications-hygiene rule applied explicitly (no panel feedback, no strategic-positioning decisions, no framing under deliberation).

HALTED on ship (disable-model-invocation: true in frontmatter), mirroring /respond-to-referees. Both skills should un-halt together once a real R&R round provides smoke-test material for the CoVe verification path. Explicit invocation via /reply-to-editor still works for early testing.

Output destination convention matches the submissions spoke: skill writes to working/cover_letter_<journal>_R<round>.tex; once Kai reviews and approves, the file is promoted manually to project_management/submissions/<NN_journal_round>/overleaf/cover_letter.tex for the journal-portal Overleaf sync. The skill itself never auto-promotes; the human-in-the-loop step is explicit.

Templates: new templates/editor-cover-letter.md (the document shape). Cross-references shared with /respond-to-referees: rules/post-flight-verification.md, agents/claim-verifier.md, rules/latex-fragment-conventions.md.

docs.title: 2026-06-23 — New skill /meeting-notes (project-workflow v1.38.0)
docs.text:
New skill for turning a meeting transcript (Teams/Zoom .vtt export, written notes .md, or pasted text) into a structured note under project_management/notes_and_feedback/<YYYY-MM-DD>_<kind>_<id>.md + extracted action items appended to project_management/TODO.md. Built after a survey of academic-economist meeting-notes setups (Blattman's /post-meeting on claudeblattman.com is the closest reference; J-PAL's "RA documents every decision" handbook discipline informs the template).

Architecture.

  • Two-pass extraction is the load-bearing design. Pass 1 emits candidates (decision / action_item / open_question) each anchored by a verbatim transcript quote; candidates without a quote are discarded. Pass 2 promotes and tags, surfacing uncertainty explicitly: [OWNER NOT NAMED], [DATE NOT NAMED], [DECISION TENTATIVE]. The user resolves at review time. Pattern drawn from the LLM-meeting-summarisation literature on phantom action items and mid-conversation decision misses.
  • Helper script (scripts/extract.py) handles the deterministic bits: VTT timestamp/voice-tag parsing, attendee extraction from speaker labels, date hint from VTT header, filename generation (YYYY-MM-DD_<kind>_<identifier>.md), confidentiality blocklist check, SHA-256 provenance footer, structured TODO.md append with backlinks to the note file. Two subcommands: parse and write.
  • Confidentiality gate refuses to write without explicit user confirmation when the transcript path or content matches the standard blocklist (referee/reviewer/panel/grades/medical/hiring). Mirrors Kai's standing git add blocklist; on confirm, prepends the note with a <!-- CONFIDENTIAL -- do not commit to git --> banner.

Privacy default. Local-only by design. Accepts only local files + pasted text; no third-party API calls. Documented capture path is Teams/Zoom native transcript export (keeps the recording inside the institutional data agreement). Granola is explicitly NOT supported because its notes default to publicly-shareable-by-link (documented public-by-default link issue; not FERPA-compliant) and the cost of accidentally sharing referee/panel content is high. Future enhancement: native ms365-MCP Teams transcript fetch when the MCP is detected.

Argument shape modeled on Blattman's /done: meeting-notes <transcript> [date:YYYY-MM-DD] [kind:meeting|call|feedback|decision] [identifier:slug] [project:name] [--no-todo].

Not built yet (queued): /weekly-review companion for cross-meeting synthesis. Shipping the per-meeting skill first mirrors Blattman's shipped order; the synthesis layer's design depends on having an accumulated note corpus.

Smoke-tested end-to-end on a synthetic Teams VTT: speaker turns parsed (<v Name> voice tags), attendees extracted, date hint pulled from header, filename generated; blocklist correctly fires triple match on a referee-transcript fixture; write subcommand produces the note file with provenance footer + TODO.md append with backlinks + uncertainty summary (missing_owner, missing_date, tentative_decisions).

docs.title: 2026-06-23 — /lit-corpus hybrid 3-tier PDF engine (project-workflow v1.37.0)
docs.text:
/lit-corpus now supports three PDF conversion engines via --engine:

  • marker (new default) — marker-pdf. Recovers regression-table cell structure, inline LaTeX math, typed figure captions. ~10s/page on CPU, ~25 pages/s on GPU. First-run downloads ~1 GB of layout/OCR/table models from HuggingFace (cached under ~/.cache/datalab).
  • fast (alias pymupdf4llm, the previous default) — kept as an opt-in for quick incremental adds. ~0.1s/page, but loses table structure and math fidelity.
  • mistral — Mistral OCR API for scanned / image-only PDFs. ~$0.001/page, requires MISTRAL_API_KEY. Selected automatically as a fallback when the primary engine produces <500 bytes of text (the near-empty signal that almost always means a scanned PDF with no text layer). Fallback only fires if the env var is set; otherwise the "possible scan" warning fires as before.

Driven by a survey of 11 PDF→markdown tools (marker, docling, nougat, GROBID, Mistral OCR, unstructured.io, MarkItDown, pdfplumber, pymupdf, Granite-Docling-258M, pymupdf4llm itself) against pdfmux's 200-PDF benchmark and the level-up benchmark. Marker won on the dimensions that matter for econ workflows (regression tables, math, figure captions), with Mistral OCR strictly better on math (94.29%) and scanned docs (98.96%) where it earns its keep. Nougat is unmaintained since Aug 2023 and explicitly NOT used.

Output post-processing (header/footer stripping, JSTOR boilerplate, references trimming, metadata extraction, index generation, SHA-256 incremental caching) is unchanged — only the PDF→markdown front end was factored. Existing flags (--bib, --recursive, --force, --keep-references) behave identically.

literature.md docs page (in working/principles-drafts) gains a "What the conversion captures and what it loses" section split into "permanently lost regardless of tool" (raw figure pixels, colour-coded series, network topology, choropleth shading) vs "recoverable with a strong engine" (table cells, LaTeX math, typed figure captions, multi-column reading order). This ships regardless of the engine in use.

docs.title: 2026-06-23 — New top-level skill kai-pedagogical-writing v1.0
docs.text:
Sibling to kai-writing (which stays for academic / journal-paper prose). The new skill captures Kai's PEDAGOGICAL voice — docs-site pages, lecture-slide explainers, READMEs, short internal training. Distinct metric (reader understands AND can transfer the knowledge), distinct structure (transfer-learning pattern: real numbers + every reasoning step + explicit prior-concept references), distinct anti-patterns (skip-the-WHY / wall-of-text / sycophancy / leave-reader-stuck), and the same hard dash discipline (≤1 em-dash per paragraph).

Pipeline: 4 stages (Drafter A rule-first + Drafter B example-first → Critic against the 14-section style profile → Rewriter synthesizes). Stages run nested or in-role per cost. The bundled pedagogical_style_kai.md is the load-bearing reference; SKILL.md and profile must agree, profile wins. Boundary clear in the description: NOT for journal-paper prose (kai-writing), NOT for slide design (research-presentation), NOT for blog/op-ed (no skill yet — would route through kai-writing for now if asked).

Iteration-1 eval (3 cases × 2 configurations, 6 runs). Pass rate 24/24 with skill vs. 20/24 baseline (+17 pp). All 4 baseline failures clustered on the style markers Kai explicitly called out: em-dash discipline (parenthetical-pair "— X — but Y" patterns), voice-register mix ("you" only, no "we" or "I"), and first-person stance. Baseline content substance was strong in both configurations — concrete numbers, prior-concept callouts, multi-step reasoning all passed without the skill. Cost: ~2.6× wall time (the 4-stage pipeline is the design), ~31% more tokens per run. Workspace + viewer artifacts live in a sibling skills/kai-pedagogical-writing-workspace/ (gitignored).

docs.title: 2026-06-18 — Research figure titles: descriptive default (r-research-workflow v1.3.1)
docs.text: Second research-vs-teaching divergence resolved (Kai's call). Research-paper figures now default to a descriptive title — variable + unit + period ("Battle deaths by country, 2018–2024") — with the finding argued in the body text, not baked into the figure (a conclusion in a results figure's title reads as editorializing to a referee). Narrative finding-titles remain the teaching / public-facing-explainer convention. Updated figure-design-rules §1.2 + §9.1 (the canonical rule the r-reviewer agent enforces via the 8-point checklist — r-reviewer has no title-check of its own, so it inherits this), coef-plot (3 spots), and — in the top-level real-data-figure skill — §1 + the self-check + a research-paper caveat on owid-design-principles. Scope call (flagged for veto): real-data-figure keeps narrative titles available for policy-brief / public-facing figures rather than banning them outright.

docs.title: 2026-06-18 — Research house palette research_pal (r-research-workflow v1.3.0)
docs.text: After a research-vs-teaching colour review (Kai's point: I'd wrongly inferred teaching colours should carry into research), _theme.R gains research_pal — a strong, high-contrast, brand-free paper palette (blue #1F4E8C, red #C8102E, teal #0A7E8C, gold #E1A100, purple #6A3D9A, grey #4D4D4D) plus scale_colour_research() / scale_fill_research(). It is now the default for research figures; Okabe-Ito is retained as the colour-blind-safe fallback (>4 categories / accessibility-critical). The rationale is the research-vs-teaching divergence: a paper has no brand, so colour is functional — the first four hues separate in greyscale (referees print B&W) and for common colour-blindness. figure-design-rules §9.5 and map-figure §6b updated to match (research_pal categorical; warm YlOrRd or viridis sequential; the USG brand ramps are explicitly teaching-only). Palette approved by Kai off rendered swatches (Economist data-team + OWID informed); verified by a rendered demo (templates/examples/research_pal_demo.png).

docs.title: 2026-06-18 — _dataroot.do: shared Stata data-root anchor (project-workflow v1.34.0)
docs.text: Completes id-mining's clone-setup-marker-disconnect ask #1. The path-resolution logic that was inlined in 00_setup.do is extracted into a new templates/_dataroot.do — the single definition of $ROOT / $DATAROOT / $rawdata / $processed / $documentation / $code / $output / $paper (marker-first .data-in-parent re-anchor). 00_setup.do now sources it (locating it whether run from the project root or code/); 01_*/02_* inherit via do 00_setup.do, and a custom build do-file that needs only the data globals can do _dataroot.do directly. That ends the per-file path-ladder drift that blocked a new co-author (a builder honoured the marker while 01/02 used a hard-coded per-user cd ladder). _dataroot.do does not clear, so it is safe to source mid-pipeline. Verified: the full template harness is 23/23 green (R + Python + Stata, cases C1–C7 incl. run-from-code/ and detached-HEAD) after the refactor; the harness now copies _dataroot.do into the sandbox.

docs.title: 2026-06-18 — check-clone-discipline: per-clone .data-in-parent marker check (project-workflow v1.33.0)
docs.text: Closes the load-bearing half of id-mining's clone-setup-marker-disconnect report: a new co-author was blocked because a clone with no .data-in-parent marker resolves data only through the legacy per-user cap cd path ladder. check_clone_discipline.py now scans every deployed clone (clone_<XX>/ and legacy code_<XX>/) for the marker and emits a "Clone setup" advisory naming the offenders, with the fix (touch .data-in-parent) and the why. Wired into both paths — from inside a clone (raises a clean OK_CLONE exit 0 to soft-warning 2) and at the container (AT_CONTAINER). Fixtures now model a well-formed clone (with marker) by default; test battery 32 → 40/40. Still to come (needs Stata-side verification): a lightweight shared _dataroot.do anchor + the bootstrap-project onboarding note ("run Stata only from clone_<XX>/code", touch .data-in-parent).

docs.title: 2026-06-18 — map-figure: "No data" fill footgun fixed + Kosovo ISO3 alias (skills/map-figure)
docs.text:
Hardening surfaced by test-rendering the skill on real World Bank GDP-per-capita data (a deliberate "run it, don't trust the spec" check), then reviewing the PNG:

  • No-data fill footgun fixed. The skill's own §5 example paired to_no_data_factor() (which makes "No data" a real factor level) with scale_fill_viridis_d(..., na.translate = FALSE) — which then colours "No data" viridis yellow, because na.translate cannot touch a real level. The render walked straight into it. New bundled scale_fill_map_d(x, name=…) builds an explicit manual palette (viridis for the data bins, grey for "No data"); §5, §A4 and the worked skeleton now use it. A misleading swatch is worse than silent grey.
  • Kosovo ISO3 alias. Added ne_iso_aliases (World Bank XKX → Natural Earth KOS) applied automatically in the by = "iso3" join, so a pure code-system difference no longer reports as a missing country.
  • Reproducible example added under skills/map-figure/examples/ (demo_world_gdp_pc.R + .png + source CSV) — no orphan exhibit.
  • test_map_core.R extended 6 → 8/8: the alias resolution and the grey-not-viridis no-data colouring are now regression-guarded.
  • Lecture-pipeline map style folded in (mined directly from fig2_africa_pastoralist_map.R + usg_theme.R + the Plotly create_choropleth factory, so the skill carries Kai's encoded style, not a reconstruction): the house warm conflict ramp #FFFFCC→#990000 + the USG blue/red diverging ramp (§6b — viridis stays the colour-blind-safe research default per his own figure-design-rules §9.5); the single-continent lon/lat coord_sf(xlim,ylim) option for equator-straddling maps (§3); the OWID-style continuous log colorbar with humanised breaks (§5); and white-halo geom_text_repel labels (§8).

docs.title: 2026-06-18 — guard_clutter Bash false-positive fix (project-workflow v1.32.0)
docs.text: The audit flagged that guard_clutter's Bash mode scanned every token, so a legitimate versioned source file — cp data/processed/acled_v9.csv dest/ — tripped on _v9. Now it's target-aware: for cp/mv/rsync only the destination (last positional) is checked, for mkdir every positional, and redirects flag their target file. Versioned/dated source files in data pipelines no longer nag, while backup targets (paper_backup.tex, _ORIG/, draft_v2.tex) still ask. 25-case smoke test green (+3 versioned-source cases).

docs.title: 2026-06-18 — coord: move-proof .coord-session marker (coord v0.2.0)
docs.text: Closes uam's Q3. The coord session-name resolver relied on session_name_by_cwd, which silently broke when a project moved/renamed in Dropbox (uam's Research/UAM → understanding_artisinal_mining). Now a .coord-session marker file in the project (or any parent) — first non-empty non-# line = the short-name — resolves the session name above the CWD map (below only the CLAUDE_COORD_SESSION_NAME env override). The project carries its own identity, so a rename can't misroute it. SKILL.md + command resolution order updated in sync; refuse-message now suggests the marker.

docs.title: 2026-06-18 — clone-CLAUDE.md thin-stub model (project-workflow v1.31.0)
docs.text:
In the leaderless multi-clone layout, the container's loose CLAUDE.md is the single canonical project doc. The repo-TRACKED clone_<XX>/CLAUDE.md copies were allowed to be full mirrors — and full mirrors drift from the container as the rules evolve, with nothing keeping them in sync. They now become thin LOUD pointer stubs.

  • New template templates/clone-CLAUDE-stub.md (~15 lines, brand-neutral, matches clone-readme.md's tone): a loud header that THIS file is a per-author clone marker, NOT the project rules; the canonical rules are at the container root (../CLAUDE.md) and carry every hard rule; "at session start, read ../CLAUDE.md"; and editing the rules means editing the container's CLAUDE.md, not this stub.
  • /refactor-structure --migrate-to-multi-clone Phase 6 gains step 2b: after the container CLAUDE.md defusal block is set up, each tracked clone_<XX>/CLAUDE.md is replaced with the stub (dry-run lists; --execute writes; the container's own CLAUDE.md is never touched). Phase 6 is prose-driven — there is no migrate flag in refactor_structure.py, so the wiring is an explicit prose step matching the rest of the phase.
  • Documented in principles/project-structure-canonical.md + the plugin rules mirror (canonical-vs-stub note under the multi-clone setup items), bootstrap-project §3.2a.bis, and docs/per-project-onboarding.md (a "which CLAUDE.md is the real one?" note in the clone-setup section).
  • Interim-PR note: an EXISTING multi-clone project (e.g. UAM) retires its drifting full-mirror clone CLAUDE.md via a one-time PR to main replacing the tracked clone_*/CLAUDE.md with the stub — which then reaches every clone, including co-authors who never re-run --migrate.

docs.title: 2026-06-18 — check_clone_discipline: per-container scratch allowlist (project-workflow v1.30.0)
docs.text: Closes uam's Q4: the v1.27.0 container scratch scan is advisory-only (never blocks), but it would nag about load-bearing container content — e.g. uam's transitional temp_claude/ holding pending rescue stashes. Now an optional <container>/.scratch-allow (one fnmatch glob/name per line, # comments) declares known-keep exceptions; matching entries aren't flagged. Mirrors /housekeeping's root_allow; selective (a *.pdf allow silences the PDF but temp_claude/ is still flagged); the advisory now points users to the file. 32/32 test battery green (+3 allowlist cases).

docs.title: 2026-06-18 — map-figure comprehensiveness: cartographic craft layer
docs.text:
Folded a vetted cartography research memo into skills/map-figure/ — the CORRECTNESS core (key reconciliation, the iso_a3 == "-99" trap, equal-area projection, binning, sequential-vs-diverging, dateline/ Antarctica, labels) was already solid, so this adds the CRAFT layer on top without doubling the skill:

  • §9 Normalize: rates not counts (+ proportional symbols). A choropleth fills area, so raw counts just redraw the population map — normalise to a rate before filling, with a small-denominator caveat; inherent counts go on a proportional-symbol map (scale_size_area, the area-proportional one, not scale_size).
  • §10 Map furniture & display. Scale bar / north arrow only on a single-country extent; missing data needs its OWN legend key (the silent-grey-NA bug at the display layer); graticules off by default; interactive (mapview / tmap_mode("view")) for exploration, static for print.
  • §11 Advanced layouts (pointers). Faceted small-multiples with ONE shared scale; insets (cowplot/patchwork); topology-aware generalisation (rmapshaper::ms_simplify, not st_simplify); bivariate choropleths (biscale).
  • na.value fix: the §5/§6 examples (and the map_core.R worked skeleton) used na.value = "grey85" with no legend entry; now recode NA to an explicit "No data" level. Added a lean to_no_data_factor() helper to map_core.R for exactly that.
  • Checklist + sources extended (tmap book, r-spatial "beautiful maps" Part 3, biscale, rmapshaper). test_map_core.R stays 5/5.

Repo-level skill, so no plugin.json bump.

docs.title: 2026-06-18 — Trigger-overlap fixes (project-workflow v1.29.0, r-research-workflow v1.2.2)
docs.text:
Two skill descriptions the architecture audit flagged for over-firing:

  • git-assistant was the broadest trigger in the toolkit. Trimmed bare generic verbs (status/update/sync/"what's my situation" — which fired on non-git intents like "update the table") to repo-scoped phrasing; removed the experiment-scaffolding phrases that collided with /experiment; added a defer clause (scaffolding a throwaway experiment script → /experiment; git-assistant only does the branch plumbing) and a generic-verb scoping guard.
  • /coef-plot now carries the boundary its siblings have — NOT for lecture/slide figures (the lecture-pipeline data-visualizer owns those), and choropleths route to map-figure.

docs.title: 2026-06-18 — new map-figure skill (choropleth maps in R)
docs.text:
New repo-level skill skills/map-figure/ for publication-quality choropleth / country-level maps (paper / working-paper / policy-brief contexts — NOT lecture slides, which stay on the pipeline data-visualizer). It encodes only the non-trivial map mechanics agents get wrong by default and defers the rest to siblings:

  • Country-name / ISO3 reconciliation + a LOUD anti-join — reuses the proven join core from the lecture pipeline (match_to_naturalearth()), bundled in assets/map_core.R.
  • The Natural Earth iso_a3 == "-99" trap — France/Norway/etc. carry -99, so an ISO3 join silently drops them; helper coalesces iso_a3_eh / adm0_a3 over iso_a3 (ne_iso_code()).
  • Equal-area projection per region (Equal Earth world / LAEA Europe / Albers US / Africa), resolving the map_core-vs-§6 Robinson contradiction in favour of Equal Earth for choropleths.
  • Binning for skewed data (jenks/quantile/log10, stated in caption), sequential-vs-diverging fill, antimeridian/Antarctica handling, and st_point_on_surface() direct labels.

Defers data sourcing → data-catalog; naming/saving/source-line/1–5 scoring → real-data-figure; theme/palette → theme_research() + Okabe-Ito. Updated real-data-figure's choropleth-routing line to point here. Repo-level skill, so no plugin.json bump.

docs.title: 2026-06-18 — Rule-scoping fixes from the architecture audit (project-workflow v1.28.0)
docs.text:
An adversarial audit of skill/trigger overlap and rule scoping found two auto-attach bugs (same class as the v1.25.0 coding-workflow fix):

  • migration-discipline.md had no paths: frontmatter — so the "resilient paths during a layout change" rule could never auto-load. Added **/*.do, **/*.R, **/*.py, code/** (plugin mirror + principles/ master).
  • model-routing.md listed **/*.md — auto-attaching an agent/skill routing rule to every markdown file in every project (pure always-on noise). Removed it; kept only agents/**/*.md + skills/**/SKILL.md.

The audit's larger findings (skill-trigger disambiguations; whether high-cost conventions need to be hooks; and the sub-agent-bypass question — do PreToolUse hooks fire on a delegated sub-agent's tool calls?) are tracked separately.

docs.title: 2026-06-18 — check_clone_discipline detects scratch at the shared container root (project-workflow v1.27.0)
docs.text:
Closes the v1.20.0 queued item: the script judged WHERE the session runs but never looked at WHAT junk had piled up at the inert shared container. That is the id-mining failure mode — sessions run AT the container deposit temp_claude/, stray *.log, build PDFs, and a retired code_<XX>/ clone name at the root instead of inside a clone.

  • New scan_container_scratch() flags four categories at the container root: temp_claude/ (should be per-clone), stray *.log, build artifacts (*.pdf / *.aux / *.synctex.gz), and retired code_<XX>/ clone names (rename to clone_<XX>/). Excludes the legitimate singletons (data/, literature/, project_management/, paper/, clone_<XX>/, CLAUDE.md, README, .gitignore, .claude/); each category capped at 10.
  • Runs whenever the container is known — from inside a clone (parent = container) OR AT_CONTAINER — and APPENDS a "Container hygiene" advisory naming the findings + the fix ("the container is inert; move scratch into your clone or delete it; rename code_/ to clone_/").
  • ADVISORY only: never turns a clean OK_CLONE into a hard stop; at most raises a clean exit 0 to soft-warning exit 2. The five verdicts and their exit codes are unchanged. ASCII-only output (Windows cp1252 console).
  • New test_check_clone_discipline.py battery (29 checks, spaced-path temp fixtures) green: all five verdict classes + the scratch cases and the clean-container / canonical-clone controls that must NOT warn.

docs.title: 2026-06-18 — Portability: core conventions travel in every project CLAUDE.md (project-workflow v1.26.0)
docs.text:
The eval showed the conventions were carried by the user's global ~/.claude/CLAUDE.md + plugin agent descriptions, not the project files — so a co-author without that global config could miss them. Fix: make the project's own CLAUDE.md (always loaded, for everyone) carry the hard rules.

  • CLAUDE-template.md gains a mandatory "Core conventions (always apply — do NOT delete)" block right after Project mode: (1) raw-data read-only, (2) version-with-git-not-copies, (3) one-canonical-file + /experiment, (4) exhibits-trace-to-code incl. output/figures_external/ for non-code assets, (5) scratch-is-disposable. The hook-backed ones say so.
  • Closes two real holes: raw-read-only previously lived only inside the multi-clone block (which single-clone projects delete), and figures_external wasn't mentioned anywhere in the template.
  • bootstrap-project §3.1 marks the block mandatory for every project; the repo-structure diagram now shows output/figures_external/.

docs.title: 2026-06-18 — coding-workflow.md now auto-attaches (project-workflow v1.25.0)
docs.text:
An empirical eval (4 fresh agents, realistic tasks in a throwaway research-project fixture) showed behaviour was correct 4/4 — but for a revealing reason: the conventions were carried by the global ~/.claude/CLAUDE.md + the plugin agent descriptions, NOT by the project rule files. coding-workflow.md — the file that holds the canonical-file / no-_v2 / experimentation rule — had no paths: frontmatter, so it could never auto-load when editing code.

  • Added paths: (**/*.do, **/*.R, **/*.py, code/**) to both the plugin mirror and the principles/ master, so the rule auto-attaches on code edits.
  • This is necessary but not sufficient: the deeper portability fix — putting the core conventions in the bootstrap-project-generated project CLAUDE.md so a co-author gets them without the user's personal global config — is queued.
  • Verify in a real session with /memory (lists the rules actually loaded).

docs.title: 2026-06-17 — guard_clutter hook: stop versioning-by-copying (project-workflow v1.24.0)
docs.text:
The bullet-proof layer for the clutter problem. Soft rules couldn't stop an agent from filling a project with paper_backup_*/, _ORIG, _pre_rerun_*, draft_v2, and one-off _*.py — so this is a deterministic gate, the same shape as the raw-data guard.

  • guard_clutter PreToolUse hook asks before creating a backup / snapshot / version-suffixed copy — a Write to a path like paper_backup_2026-06-02/, 02_analysis_ORIG.do, draft_v2.tex, results_final.do, _paper_new/, or a Bash cp/mv/mkdir/rsync/redirect whose target carries a backup/version/date marker. It returns an ask (not a block) and points to the right home: a git branch for safety, temp_claude/ for scratch, /experiment (code/_exploratory/) for an experiment, .claude/legacy/ to park something recoverable.
  • Exempts the sanctioned homes (.claude/legacy/, temp_claude/, _archive/, old/, .git/) so archiving correctly is never nagged.
  • Fences the day-archive escape hatch in coding-workflow.md: dated copies only when git is genuinely unavailable, and into .claude/legacy/ (which the guard exempts), never code/ siblings.
  • 22-case smoke test green (hooks/guard_clutter_smoke_test.sh).

docs.title: 2026-06-17 — /build-exhibits-preview becomes a bare-bones copy of the paper (project-workflow v1.23.0)
docs.text:
The exhibits preview is now the artifact you actually want to review figures in: a bare-bones version of the real paper — its real preamble, its real section/subsection skeleton (titles kept, prose stripped), and every exhibit with its notes — auto-compiled and opened in your desktop PDF app. Previously it was a flat list of exhibits under a "nearest section title" with a hardcoded minimal preamble; now each exhibit sits in its true structural context.

  • Real preamble. build_exhibits_preview.py borrows the paper's OWN preamble: it resolves \input{...preamble...} relative to the paper (and prepends the main file's \documentclass if the standalone preamble lacks one), else lifts everything from \documentclass to \begin{document} out of the main .tex. The preview's helper macros (\interp/\trans/\fignote/ \safeincludegraphics) are always appended, guarded so there is never a double \documentclass. Falls back to the minimal preamble only if neither strategy works; the report states which strategy was used.
  • Real heading skeleton. Every \section/\subsection/\subsubsection (and starred variants) is reproduced in document order via one position-sorted walk — even headings with no exhibits, so it is a true skeleton — with each exhibit placed under the heading where it appears. A minimal \title/\author/\maketitle is emitted when the paper has them.
  • Auto-compile + auto-open. --compile is now the default; on a clean compile the PDF opens in the OS default viewer (os.startfile on Windows, open/xdg-open elsewhere — best-effort, never crashes). New --no-compile and --no-open flags.
  • Preserved verbatim: inline-float detection (exit 2), the paper_structure.md plan-drift check, graceful compile-degradation (\IfFileExists guards + red [exhibit not built yet] placeholders), and the command's REQUIRED self-view defect-checklist gate before sharing.

Smoke-tested on a temp fixture (a paper.tex with \input{preamble.tex}, sections + subsections, a real \includegraphics and an \input{output/tables/...} fragment): the borrowed preamble + helper macros, a correctly ordered heading skeleton with exhibits under the right headings, and a clean 1-page PDF were all confirmed; the documentclass-lift and fallback preamble strategies and the guarded desktop-open path were verified separately.

docs.title: 2026-06-17 — /experiment: experiment-then-merge-back workflow (project-workflow v1.22.0)
docs.text:
A repeated pattern (Kai + Ronny): try new analysis in a small scratch file rather than hacking inside the long canonical file, then fold the working part back in. Now a command, with the gotchas an agent gets wrong baked in.

  • /experiment start <topic> → scaffolds one transient scratch script at code/_exploratory/exp_<topic>.{do,R,py} that sources 00_setup (so the branch-aware redirect sends its outputs to output/_exploratory/<branch>/ and the canonical exhibits are never touched), on a feature branch. One file, no _v2 versioning.
  • /experiment merge → folds the working code into 02_analysis as a clean bannered section, drops the duplicate 00_setup source, routes outputs through the globals, verifies the full pipeline runs, then deletes the scratch (verify-before-tidy; if it breaks, it stops and keeps the scratch).
  • code/_exploratory/ is a transient exception to the one-canonical-file rule — deleted at merge-back, so the end state is still one analysis file. coding-workflow.md gains a pointer to the command.

docs.title: 2026-06-17 — Clone README "where things go", multi-clone CLAUDE.md, talking post-merge hook (project-workflow v1.21.0)
docs.text:
Carries the inert-container knowledge to where co-authors actually meet it, and makes the compile-on-merge paper hook stop failing silently now that everyone is expected to have LaTeX.

  • Clone README tells co-authors where things go. templates/clone-readme.md gains a "Where things live (and where NOT to work)" section: the shared container is inert (never run Claude/R/Stata at the container root; stray scratch there means a session ran in the wrong place); a non-code figure (photo, hand-drawn diagram, logo) goes in your clone's output/figures_external/ then commit → push → PR (there is no output/ at the container root); the current submission PDF lives at <container>/paper/, auto-compiled from main on every merge.
  • Bootstrap propagates the multi-clone block. bootstrap-project §3.1 now states explicitly (alongside the existing §3.2a.bis handling) that a multi-clone project includes the "## Multi-clone layout (intentional)" block from CLAUDE-template.md verbatim, and single-clone projects omit it — so a new co-author's generated CLAUDE.md carries the inert-container rules automatically.
  • post-merge-paper hook no longer skips silently. templates/hooks/post-merge-paper still NEVER blocks a merge (always exit 0, no set -e), but now: prints one stderr line + writes STATUS=SKIPPED_NO_LATEX when no LaTeX engine is found; prints one line, saves the compile log to <container>/paper/.last_build.log, and writes STATUS=FAILED on a failed compile; detects \includepdf and prints a tailored "grab the PDF from Overleaf/CI" line with STATUS=SKIPPED_INCLUDEPDF instead of a generic failure; and writes <container>/paper/LAST_BUILD.txt (date, ref short-SHA, engine, STATUS) on every run including success. All marker/log writes are best-effort. Smoke-tested on a temp clone fixture: OK, SKIPPED_NO_LATEX, SKIPPED_INCLUDEPDF.

docs.title: 2026-06-17 — Session hygiene + "where does a non-code figure go" docs (project-workflow v1.20.0)
docs.text:
A field finding (a teammate's container root held temp_claude/, Stata logs, and a retired code_AW/ — all symptoms of sessions run at the container root instead of inside a clone) plus a docs gap on where non-code figures live.

  • The container is inert. The multi-clone defusal block (CLAUDE-template
  • canonical spec) now states plainly: never launch Claude/R/Stata at the root; scratch there (temp_claude/, *.log, a build PDF) is a red flag to clean up and move into a clone; a retired code_<XX>/ name is an unmigrated clone. (A check_clone_discipline scan that auto-detects this is queued.)
  • New-figure docs. The FAQ gains a (deliberately open-framed) "I have a figure that isn't made by code — where does it go?" entry, and project-structure.md gains an "Adding a figure that isn't made by code" section: non-code assets go in your clone's output/figures_external/, commit → PR → others pull; there is no output/ at the container root.
  • Fixed a stale FAQ line that still described the container as holding a read-only copy of the paper (it's the compiled PDF now).

docs.title: 2026-06-17 — Container keeps a compiled paper PDF, not a mirror (project-workflow v1.19.0)
docs.text:
Replaced the container's PUBLISHED/ read-only mirror (paper/+output/+ code/) with a single paper/ folder holding the compiled PDF of main. The mirror was a redundant third copy — every clone already has the tracked sources and outputs from main. What's actually wanted at the container is one obvious, Dropbox-synced place to grab the current paper PDF for submission.

  • templates/hooks/post-merge-publish → renamed post-merge-paper. On every git merge origin/main it exports main's paper/ (+output/ for figures), compiles (latexmk preferred so citations resolve; pdflatex fallback), and copies only the PDF to <container>/paper/ with a PAPER_README.md.
  • Graceful — never blocks a merge. No LaTeX, or a failed compile (e.g. the \includepdf bare-compile gotcha) → skip silently, leave the previous PDF. Refresh happens on whichever machine can compile main cleanly.
  • No binary in git, no manual step, leaderless. Verified end-to-end (minimal paper → container/paper/paper.pdf; no-LaTeX PATH exits 0).
  • Canonical spec + co-author onboarding updated; the old mirror is gone.

docs.title: 2026-06-17 — Fix MOVE-mode nesting bug in /refactor-structure (project-workflow v1.18.0)
docs.text:
A latent bug surfaced while building the safety loop: when a canonical directory was both a safe-rename target and pre-created in phase 1 — directly (e.g. code) or as a parent of a created child (code/prompts) — the phase-2 git mv scripts code nested the source inside it, landing files at code/scripts/.

  • build_plan now drops exact rename-target dirs from creates.
  • apply_plan skips creating a dir equal to a safe target, and defers creating canonical children under a target (code/prompts) until after the rename lands — so the move reaches the target flat and the empty children still get scaffolded.
  • COPY mode (dirs_exist_ok merge) was already correct; the version-bump caught up the field, which had drifted to 1.16.0 while the description carried 1.17.0.
  • Verified on four fixtures: scripts→code MOVE (flat, code/prompts deferred), scripts→code COPY (flat, original preserved), raw→data/raw nested-target (flat), and a no-rename baseline (all canonical dirs created).
